title: Three letters, then a long run of stories.
subtitle: Pausing before a surah full of warnings
then: This surah came in the middle Makkan years, when the Prophet ﷺ was being called a poet and a sorcerer. It opens with three letters, Ta Sin Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What follows is a long series of stories about people who were shown signs and still refused.
now: You open the app between two notifications, half your mind still on the email you did not answer. Before the stories begin, there are three letters you cannot explain. {idea}A small speed bump.{/idea} A chance to put the phone face down and actually arrive.
old: I need to understand every word before it can do anything for me.
new: Some words exist to make me stop, notice, and listen to what comes next.
try: Before you read today, take three slow breaths and silence your phone first.

title: A Book that draws a clear line.
subtitle: What clear means in this surah

row.title: it is too unclear
sub: that is why I hold back

then: The people of Makkah said the message was poetry or magic. This verse answers first: these are verses of {idea}a clear Book{/idea}, one that separates truth from falsehood and guidance from misguidance. The rest of the surah shows that people refused it, not because it was unclear.
now: You tell yourself you will start praying on time once you understand everything better. You have watched hours of videos about it. {trap}The fog is not always in the message.{/trap} Sometimes the instruction is clear, and the delay is yours.
old: If it were clearer, I would already be doing it.
new: The Book is clear. What I do with that clarity is the real test.
try: Pick one thing you already know is right and have been delaying. Do it once today.

title: You were never meant to carry their choices.
subtitle: Allah consoles His Messenger ﷺ in his grief

row.title: the Prophet ﷺ
sub: eager for them to be guided

then: The Prophet ﷺ was so keen for his people to be guided that the grief was wearing him down. Ibn Kathir says this verse is {reward}Allah consoling His Messenger{/reward} for those who would not believe, like the verse telling him not to destroy himself in sorrow for them.
now: Your brother stopped praying years ago. Every family dinner you push, then lie awake replaying it. {trap}You have made his heart your project.{/trap} {idea}Your part is to love him and speak well.{/idea} The rest was never in your hands.
old: If someone I love does not change, I have failed.
new: I can care deeply and still let Allah hold what only He can hold.
try: Make one sincere dua for someone you worry about, then let tonight be calm.

title: Allah could force every neck to bow. He chose not to.
subtitle: Faith only counts when it is chosen
then: Quraysh kept demanding a sign that would settle things. Ibn Kathir explains: Allah could send a sign that would {idea}force them to believe{/idea}, but He does not, because {reward}He wants no one to believe except by choice.{/reward}
now: You wish Allah would just send you a sign. A dream, a voice, a moment so loud you could not doubt again. But a faith that is forced is not yours. {idea}The quiet choice you make each morning is the thing He wants.{/idea}
old: If Allah wanted me to believe more, He would show me something undeniable.
new: The freedom to choose is the gift. My choosing is what makes it worth something.
try: Tomorrow morning, before checking anything, choose to say one dua on purpose.

title: Every new reminder, the same turned back.
subtitle: A habit of turning away
then: Each time new revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ, many in Makkah turned away. Ibn Kathir notes this was the pattern with every nation: {trap}most people turn away from each new reminder.{/trap} The verse names the sender: {reward}the Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: Your friend forwards a short reminder in the group chat. You swipe it away without reading. A khutbah topic hits close, and you start thinking about lunch. {trap}Turning away becomes automatic.{/trap} {idea}Each reminder is mercy knocking.{/idea}
old: I have heard this before, so it is not for me.
new: A reminder from the Most Merciful is mercy, even when it is familiar.
try: The next reminder someone sends you, read it fully before replying or scrolling.

title: What they laughed at will come back as news.
subtitle: Mockery has a delayed answer

row.title: laughing makes it false
sub: if it is a joke, it is safe

then: Quraysh did not only reject the message. They {trap}ridiculed it{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains that they will {idea}come to know the consequences of that denial after a while{/idea}, and links it to the surah's last verse about wrongdoers learning where they end up.
now: Someone at work rolls their eyes when you step out to pray, and you laugh along to fit in. Or you make a joke about something sacred because it gets a reaction. {trap}A laugh does not change what is true.{/trap} It only changes how you will feel when you see it.
old: If I make it a joke, I do not have to take it seriously.
new: Mocking something real does not shrink it. It only delays the moment I meet it.
try: Next time a joke about faith comes up, simply do not join in.

title: They asked for a sign. The ground was full of them.
subtitle: Every noble kind growing from the earth
then: The people demanded a sign from the sky. The verse points them to the ground. Ibn Kathir says Allah tells those who opposed His Messenger ﷺ that He is the One who {idea}created the earth and made every good kind of crop, fruit and animal grow{/idea} in it.
now: You walk past the market stall of mangoes, the green strip by the bus stop, a dog asleep in the sun. You are waiting for some big moment to feel faith. {reward}It is growing on your street.{/reward} You just have not looked.
old: I would believe more if I saw something extraordinary.
new: The ordinary things growing around me are the extraordinary sign.
try: Hold one piece of fruit today and look at it for ten seconds before eating.

title: The sign was there. Most still did not believe.
subtitle: The first refrain, after the living earth

row.title: most did not
sub: the sign was not the problem

then: This line will repeat after every story in the surah. Here it follows the living earth. Ibn Kathir says the growing earth is {idea}evidence of the power of the Creator{/idea}, yet despite that {trap}the majority do not believe.{/trap}
now: Your phone has a gallery of sunsets and your kid's first steps. You saved them because they moved you. Then you closed the app. {idea}Moved is not the same as changed.{/idea} The sign did its part.
old: Being amazed by creation is the same as having faith.
new: A sign is an invitation. Most people admire it and still walk past.
try: Next time something in nature moves you, say Subhan Allah out loud before moving on.

title: Mighty enough to end it. Merciful enough to wait.
subtitle: Two names that close each story
then: The surah's second refrain. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah is {idea}Mighty{/idea}, with power to subdue all things, and {reward}Merciful{/reward}, because He does not hurry to punish the one who sins but gives him time to repent. Sa'id bin Jubayr said He is merciful to those who turn back to Him.
now: You did something last year you are still ashamed of, and nothing fell on you. Part of you decided it did not matter. {reward}The quiet is not indifference. It is time given.{/reward} The door you think is closed has been held open.
old: If nothing bad happened, Allah must not mind.
new: The time I have been given is His mercy, waiting for me to turn back.
try: Say astaghfirullah tonight for one specific thing, by name.

title: The first story begins with a call to Musa.
subtitle: Sent to the wrongdoing people
then: After the earth's signs, the surah turns to stories. Ibn Kathir describes how Allah {idea}called Musa from the side of the mountain{/idea}, spoke with him, chose him and sent him to Fir'awn and his people. Their description comes first: {trap}wrongdoing people.{/trap}
now: You see something wrong at work. A manager humiliating the new hire, a number fudged on a report. You think someone else will say something. {idea}Sometimes the call to stand up comes to you, not to someone braver.{/idea}
old: Standing up to wrong is for people more qualified than me.
new: When the call comes to me, it is because I was the one sent.
try: Notice one small unfairness today and say one honest, kind sentence about it.

title: Will they not fear Allah? A question, not a curse.
subtitle: The door left open for Fir'awn's people
then: Allah names the people: {trap}the people of Fir'awn{/trap}, who were oppressing the Children of Israel. Then comes a question, not a verdict: {idea}will they not fear Allah?{/idea} Even to them, a messenger is being sent.
now: There is someone you have written off. An ex-friend, a relative who hurt you. In your head their story is already over. {reward}Allah sent a messenger even to Fir'awn's people.{/reward} The question was still open for them.
old: Some people are too far gone to bother with.
new: If Allah left a question open for them, I can leave a little room too.
try: Think of someone you have written off and make a short dua for their guidance.

title: Even a prophet said: I am afraid.
subtitle: Musa tells his Lord his fear honestly
then: Musa does not pretend. His first words after the command are {trap}My Lord, I fear they will deny me.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Musa {idea}asked Allah to remove these difficulties{/idea} for him, as he did in Surah Ta Ha when he asked for his chest to be opened.
now: You have the job interview, the hard talk with your parents, the presentation tomorrow. You tell everyone you are fine. {idea}You can tell Allah you are scared.{/idea} Musa did, and the mission still went ahead.
old: Admitting fear means I do not trust Allah enough.
new: Telling Allah exactly what I fear is part of trusting Him.
try: Tonight, tell Allah in plain words one fear you have about tomorrow.

title: Tight chest, slow tongue. So send my brother too.
subtitle: Asking for help is part of the mission
then: Musa names his weaknesses: {trap}his chest tightens and his tongue is not fluent.{/trap} Then he asks for a solution: {reward}send for Harun.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links this to Ta Ha, where Musa asks for ease and is told his request is granted.
now: You took on the community event, the family move, the project nobody else wanted. Your chest is tight and you are too proud to ask. {idea}Musa asked for his brother.{/idea} Naming what you lack and asking for help is not weakness.
old: If I need help, I am not cut out for this.
new: Knowing my limits and asking for a partner is how hard things get done.
try: Ask one person today to help with one specific part of something heavy.

title: His past was waiting for him in Egypt.
subtitle: Musa's fear of the old charge

row.title: Allah still sends him
sub: the past is not the end

then: Ibn Kathir explains the charge: Musa had {trap}killed an Egyptian{/trap}, and that was why he had fled Egypt. Now he is being sent straight back to the people who wanted him for it. He tells Allah plainly that he fears for his life.
now: You want to start teaching kids at the masjid, or speak up in the family. But there is that thing from years ago, and you are sure someone will remember. {idea}Musa's past was real, and he was still sent.{/idea}
old: My past mistakes mean I have no right to do good now.
new: My past can be named honestly and still not have the last word.
try: Write down one good thing you have held back from because of your past. Take one step.

title: No. Go, both of you. We are with you, listening.
subtitle: Allah's answer to every fear Musa named
then: Allah answers Musa's fears in one line. {idea}No{/idea}, do not be afraid of that. Harun will go too. Ibn Kathir explains being with them means {reward}His protection, care, support and help{/reward}, like the verse I am with you both, hearing and seeing.
now: You are in the car outside the hospital, or the courthouse, or the office where you will hand in your notice. Your hands are cold. {reward}Nothing about the room has changed, but you do not walk in alone.{/reward} He is listening.
old: I will go once I stop being afraid.
new: I can go while still afraid, because Allah is with me and listening.
try: Before your next hard moment, whisper: Allah is with me, He hears.

title: Two brothers walk in with one message.
subtitle: Messengers of the Lord of all the worlds
then: Allah tells both brothers to go to Fir'awn and say they are {idea}messengers of the Lord of the worlds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes it means both of us have been sent to you. Two men from an enslaved people would say this to {trap}a king who claimed to be a god.{/trap}
now: You have to tell the landlord the repairs are not legal, or tell a senior relative the plan is wrong. You feel small in the room. {idea}What you are saying does not get its weight from your size.{/idea} Truth said gently still has its weight.
old: Who am I to say this to someone so powerful?
new: What matters is whether what I carry is true, not how big I am.
try: Say one true thing today that you have been too intimidated to say, calmly.

title: The message included a demand: let them go.
subtitle: Faith that speaks up for the oppressed
then: The second half of the message is practical. Ibn Kathir explains it as: {reward}let them go, free them{/reward} from your captivity, subjugation and torture, for they are believing servants of Allah. The Children of Israel were living in {trap}humiliating torture{/trap} under Fir'awn.
now: At work, the cleaner is shouted at and nobody says anything. In the family, one cousin is always the one blamed. {idea}Faith is not only what you believe in private.{/idea} It also asks who around you is being crushed, and whether you will speak.
old: My religion is about my prayers, not about how others are treated.
new: Standing up for someone being crushed is part of the message too.
try: Do one small thing today for someone who is usually overlooked or mistreated.

title: Fir'awn answers truth with: I raised you.
subtitle: Using past favors to silence someone
then: Fir'awn does not answer the message. He {trap}turned away and ignored him{/trap}, Ibn Kathir says, with scorn, and changed the subject: we raised you in our home and on our bed, fed you, did you favors for years. Musa grew up in Fir'awn's house.
now: You raise a concern with your boss and hear: after everything I have done for you. A parent says: I paid for your degree, so you do not get an opinion. {trap}A past favor is being turned into a gag.{/trap} Gratitude is real. So is the question that was asked.
old: If they helped me before, I have no right to disagree now.
new: I can be grateful for a favor and still say what is true.
try: Notice if you ever remind someone of your favors to win an argument. Drop it once.

title: Then he brought up the worst thing Musa ever did.
subtitle: Dragging up the past to win the present

row.title: the actual message
sub: Lord of the worlds, free them

then: Fir'awn names the killing: {trap}you did your deed{/trap}. Then the label: one of the ungrateful. Ibn Kathir says this means one who denies favors. He is still not answering the message. He is putting Musa's past on trial instead.
now: In the family argument, someone says: and what about what you did in 2019? Suddenly the real issue is gone and everyone is talking about you. {trap}Changing the subject to your past is a way to avoid the point.{/trap}
old: If they bring up my past, I have lost the argument.
new: My past can be real and the point I am making can still be true.
try: In your next disagreement, stay on the issue itself and do not bring up old faults.

title: Musa does not deny it. Yes, I did it.
subtitle: Owning a past mistake without excuses
then: Musa's answer is short. {idea}I did it then, when I was in error.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains that this was {trap}before revelation was sent{/trap} to him and before Allah made him a prophet. He does not lie, and he does not argue about it.
now: Someone brings up how you used to be. The parties, the lies, the way you treated a friend. You feel the heat rise. {idea}You can say: yes, that was me, and I was lost then.{/idea} No speech needed. It takes the weapon out of their hand.
old: I need to defend my past or hide it.
new: I can own my past honestly, because I am not who I was then.
try: Think of one past mistake you get defensive about. Say to yourself: yes, that was me then.

title: I ran. Then my Lord gave me something new.
subtitle: The past chapter closed, a new one opened
then: Musa admits he {trap}fled out of fear.{/trap} Then he points to what Allah did: {reward}granted him wisdom and made him one of the messengers.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says Musa means the first situation ended and another took its place.
now: You dropped out, lost the job, left the marriage. In your head you are still the person who ran. {reward}But Allah can turn the person who fled into the one sent back with something good.{/reward} The worst chapter does not have to be the last one.
old: The worst thing I did is who I really am.
new: Allah can close an old chapter and give me a new role.
try: Write one sentence about who you are now that your old self could not have written.

title: You raised one boy and enslaved his whole people.
subtitle: Musa weighs the favor against the harm
then: Musa turns Fir'awn's argument around. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}is there any comparison{/idea} between your favors to one man among them and {trap}the evil you have done to all of them?{/trap} The favor to Musa came out of a system that crushed his people.
now: The company gives you a bonus and a team lunch, while the contract workers are underpaid. Someone gives generously to your cause and treats their staff badly. {idea}Kindness to you does not erase harm to others.{/idea}
old: They have been good to me, so I should not question what they do to others.
new: A favor to me does not cancel injustice to many.
try: Ask yourself if loyalty to someone is keeping you quiet about how they treat others.

title: And what is this Lord of the worlds?
subtitle: Fir'awn's question was really a denial

row.title: Fir'awn
sub: I know no god but me

then: Fir'awn used to tell his people {trap}I know not that you have a god other than me{/trap}, and he fooled them into obeying. Ibn Kathir explains that his question was not curiosity about Allah's nature. He {trap}denied that the Creator existed at all{/trap}, and meant: who is this Lord besides me?
now: You ask: but why does Allah let this happen? Sometimes it is a real question and you want the answer. Sometimes it is a door you have already shut, said as a question. {idea}Ask honestly.{/idea} A question asked with a closed heart is not looking for an answer.
old: Every question I ask about faith is just honest searching.
new: A question can be a search or a wall. I should know which one I am asking.
try: Take one doubt you have and look into it today, honestly wanting the answer.

title: Musa points up, down, and everything between.
subtitle: The Lord of the heavens and the earth

row.title: a heart seeking certainty
sub: if you seek to be sure

then: Musa does not describe Allah's essence. He points to His works: {idea}the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all between them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir lists the stars, oceans, mountains, winds and birds, all {reward}submitting and humbling themselves{/reward} before Him. If you seek certainty, it is there.
now: You are stuck in traffic, staring at the brake lights. Look up: clouds moving, a bird crossing, a sky you did not make. {idea}The proof Musa gave is right outside your window.{/idea} The question is whether you want to be sure.
old: I need a clever argument before I can feel sure.
new: The heavens and earth answer the question if I really want an answer.
try: Step outside for two minutes today and look up. Just look.

title: Do you hear this? Fir'awn turns to the crowd.
subtitle: Mockery as a way to avoid answering
then: Fir'awn had no answer. Ibn Kathir says he turned to {trap}the chiefs and leaders around him{/trap} and, mocking, said: do you not hear? Meaning, are you not amazed at this man claiming {trap}you have a god other than me{/trap}?
now: Someone makes a fair point in the group chat, and instead of replying, you screenshot it to another chat with a laughing emoji. {trap}You did not answer it. You found an audience.{/trap} That is the Fir'awn move, small size.
old: If people laugh with me, I must be right.
new: Rallying an audience is not the same as having an answer.
try: Next time you disagree with someone, reply to them directly instead of mocking them to others.

title: Your Lord, and the Lord of your forefathers.
subtitle: Musa speaks to the crowd about their own origins
then: Fir'awn turned to the crowd, so Musa answers the crowd. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}the One Who created you and your forefathers{/idea}, those who came before Fir'awn and his time. {trap}A god who was born recently{/trap} cannot be the Lord of those who lived before him.
now: The thing you treat as everything, the boss, the follower count, the career, did not exist when your grandmother was praying. It will not exist when your grandchildren are. {idea}Your Lord was Lord before all of it.{/idea}
old: What controls my life right now is what really matters.
new: Anything that came after my grandparents cannot be my Lord.
try: Call or message a grandparent or elder today and ask what they relied on in hard times.

title: Out of answers, Fir'awn calls him mad.
subtitle: Name-calling when the argument is lost
then: Fir'awn mocks the messenger as {trap}your messenger who has been sent to you{/trap}, then calls him a madman. Ibn Kathir explains Fir'awn meant there is no sense in claiming {trap}any god other than me.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ was being called mad in Makkah too.
now: You hear it in the comments: he is crazy, she is unhinged, ignore them. Sometimes you are the one typing it. {idea}When you reach for a label instead of an answer, notice that.{/idea}
old: Calling someone crazy settles the matter.
new: An insult usually means the argument has run out.
try: Catch yourself once today before calling someone stupid or crazy, and answer their point instead.

title: Lord of the sunrise and the sunset. Can Fir'awn swap them?
subtitle: Musa calmly answers the insult with more proof
then: Called a madman, Musa does not insult back. He says {idea}Lord of the east and the west.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: if Fir'awn is truly your lord, let him make the sun set in the east and rise in the west, like Ibrahim's challenge to the king. {reward}If you did but understand.{/reward}
now: Your cousin calls you a fanatic at the wedding. Everyone looks. You could snap back. {idea}Musa answered an insult with a sunrise.{/idea} A calm, clear reply often lands better than a sharp one.
old: When someone insults me, I have to hit back to keep my dignity.
new: Staying calm and reasonable when insulted is its own kind of strength.
try: The next time someone is rude to you, answer with one calm sentence and stop there.

title: Lose the debate, reach for the prison.
subtitle: Fir'awn turns from argument to threat
then: Ibn Kathir titles this part: after the rational proof, {trap}Fir'awn resorts to force.{/trap} When proof had been established against him clearly, he threatened prison, thinking there would be {trap}no further room for discussion.{/trap}
now: Your manager cannot answer your concern, so you get a warning about attitude. A parent loses the argument and says: as long as you live under my roof. {trap}When reasons run out, threats come in.{/trap} Notice it in others, and in your own voice too.
old: Whoever can punish me must be the one who is right.
new: Threats appear when reasons run out. Power and truth are different things.
try: When you have power over someone today, a child or a junior, give a reason instead of a threat.

title: Even if I show you something undeniable?
subtitle: Musa answers a threat with an offer
then: Threatened with prison, Musa does not panic or plead. He asks: even if I bring you {idea}something manifest{/idea}? Ibn Kathir explains this as {idea}clear and definitive proof.{/idea} Musa keeps the conversation on the truth.
now: You are told: stop bringing up the budget or you are off the team. You do not have to shout. You can say: what if I show you the numbers? {idea}A calm offer of evidence keeps the door open.{/idea}
old: When I am threatened, I either fight or go silent.
new: There is a third way: stay calm and keep offering what is true.
try: In a tense moment today, ask: can I show you why I think this?

title: Bring it then, if you are telling the truth.
subtitle: Fir'awn dares Musa, sure of himself
then: Fir'awn, sure of himself, says {trap}bring it forth then, if you are of the truthful.{/trap} He expects Musa to back down in front of the court. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}clear and definitive proof{/idea} is exactly what is about to arrive.
now: You have said it to someone: prove it then. You expected silence. Sometimes the proof comes, and you have to decide what to do with it. {idea}Ask only if you are ready for the answer.{/idea}
old: Daring someone to prove it shows I am confident.
new: If I ask for proof, I should be ready to accept it when it comes.
try: Think of one thing you demanded proof for. If the proof came, admit it to yourself.

title: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent.
subtitle: The first sign before the court
then: Musa threw his staff and {idea}it was a serpent, manifest.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it was very clear and obvious, {idea}with a huge body and a big mouth{/idea}, terrifying to look at. In front of the whole court, there was no room to mistake it.
now: You have something ordinary in your hand. A skill, a small salary, a free hour. It feels like just wood. {reward}What Allah does through ordinary things is not limited by how plain they look.{/reward}
old: What I have is too ordinary to matter.
new: In Allah's hands, a plain stick became the clearest sign in the room.
try: Offer one ordinary thing you have, an hour or a skill, to help someone today.

title: His hand comes out shining white for everyone.
subtitle: The second sign, visible to all

row.title: shining white
sub: like a piece of the moon

then: Musa drew his hand from his sleeve and {idea}it was white for all who looked.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it shone {idea}like a piece of the moon.{/idea} Two signs, one after another, in front of the king and his chiefs.
now: Sometimes the answer you prayed for comes, and everyone sees it. The test result, the job, the reconciliation. {idea}The question is not whether it was visible. It is what you do next.{/idea}
old: If something good is obvious, people will naturally respond to it.
new: Signs can be plain to everyone and still be rejected. My response is my part.
try: Name one clear blessing everyone around you saw this year, and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Fir'awn's spin: he is just a skilled magician.
subtitle: Relabeling a miracle to keep control

row.title: an escape
sub: so he does not have to submit

then: Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn, already doomed, {trap}hastened to stubborn denial.{/trap} He turned to his chiefs and said this is a well-versed sorcerer. He was {trap}trying to convince them it was sorcery, not a miracle.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ was called a sorcerer in Makkah too.
now: Someone you wronged forgives you, and you tell yourself they are just being fake. Your friend's life changes after she starts praying, and you say it is a phase. {trap}A label can be a way to avoid the point.{/trap}
old: If I can explain it away, I do not need to take it seriously.
new: Relabeling something true is a way of running from it.
try: Think of one good change in someone you dismissed as fake. Give it a fair second look.

title: He wants your land. Fear as a political tool.
subtitle: Fir'awn turns the chiefs against Musa
then: Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn {trap}provoked them against Musa{/trap}: he wants to win the people's hearts and take your land. Then, the man who called himself a god asks his chiefs: {trap}what do you advise?{/trap}
now: Someone at work says the new hire is after your position. A relative says that person wants to take your place in the family. {trap}Fear is the fastest way to turn people against someone.{/trap} Ask who gains from your fear.
old: If someone warns me a person is a threat, I should believe it.
new: When someone stirs up fear of another person, I should ask what they are protecting.
try: Before passing on a warning about someone, check whether it is true or just fear.

title: Delay him, and summon the whole kingdom's magicians.
subtitle: The chiefs' plan to defeat a sign
then: The chiefs advise: delay him and his brother and {trap}send callers to the cities.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn did as they suggested, {idea}which is what Allah decreed{/idea}, so that all the people would gather in one place and see the signs together in one day.
now: Someone plots against you. They go to HR, rally the family, post about you. It feels like the walls are closing in. {idea}Sometimes the very plan against you is what puts the truth in front of everyone.{/idea}
old: When people plan against me, it can only end badly.
new: Allah can turn a plot against me into the moment the truth comes out.
try: If someone is working against you, make dua for the truth to come out, and stay patient.

title: Bring every expert. Fight a miracle with experts.
subtitle: Gathering the best skill against the truth
then: The advisers want {trap}every learned, skilled magician{/trap} brought in. Ibn Kathir says the plan was to gather all the sorcerers so they would {trap}produce something like he produces{/trap} and win. They thought it was a contest of skill.
now: You are sure you can out-argue anyone, out-earn the doubts, out-plan Allah's decree. You collect expert opinions until one says what you want. {idea}Skill is a gift. It is not a weapon against what is true.{/idea}
old: With enough experts on my side, I can win any argument.
new: The best skill in the world cannot turn falsehood into truth.
try: Look for one opinion today that challenges what you want to believe, and read it fairly.

title: The day was set. The whole land would watch.
subtitle: A public appointment between truth and illusion
then: The sorcerers were assembled at {idea}a fixed time on a day appointed.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they wanted to put out the Light of Allah, but {idea}when faith and disbelief meet, faith prevails{/idea}, citing the verse: We fling the truth against falsehood and it destroys it.
now: You have a date circled on the calendar: the hearing, the meeting where it all comes out. You are scared the lie will win. {idea}Truth does not need to be louder. It needs to show up.{/idea}
old: Falsehood is louder and better organized, so it will win.
new: When truth and falsehood actually meet, truth wins.
try: Before your next hard day, make a short dua: O Allah, let the truth be clear.

title: Are you coming? The crowd is called in.
subtitle: The people gathered to watch
then: Word went out to the people: {idea}are you going to assemble?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says a great crowd came, in numbers known only to Allah. {trap}They were coming to watch a contest{/trap}, set up by the king who ruled them.
now: There is drama online: two people arguing, a big reveal. You open it to watch. {trap}You are there for the show, not the truth.{/trap} But truth can still reach the people who came just to watch.
old: I am just watching. It does not involve me.
new: Whatever I come to watch, I am still responsible for what I see.
try: Next time you open a public argument online, ask yourself what is actually true, not who won.

title: We will follow whoever wins.
subtitle: The crowd that chose sides by results
then: The people said they would follow the sorcerers {trap}if they are the winners.{/trap} Ibn Kathir points out what they did not say: {idea}we will follow the truth, whether it is with the sorcerers or with Musa.{/idea} The people simply followed the religion of their king.
now: You back the opinion that is trending, the side your friends are on, the boss most likely to promote you. {trap}You are following the winner.{/trap} The harder question is not who is winning, but who is right.
old: The side that comes out on top is usually the right one.
new: Winning and being right are different. I want to follow what is true.
try: Pick one opinion you hold because everyone around you does. Check it on its own merits.

title: Before the contest, the magicians ask about pay.
subtitle: Working for falsehood, for a fee
then: When the sorcerers reached Fir'awn's court, with its pavilion, servants and soldiers, their first concern was money. Ibn Kathir says they asked him to {trap}treat them well and bring them closer{/trap} if they won. They were there for {trap}the reward.{/trap}
now: You are offered good money to write copy you know is misleading, or to look the other way on a contract. Your first thought is the number. {trap}Skill for hire can end up working for a lie.{/trap}
old: As long as the pay is good, what I am working for does not matter much.
new: What my skill serves matters as much as what it pays.
try: Ask yourself honestly: does any part of my work serve something I know is wrong?

title: Yes, and you will sit close to me.
subtitle: Fir'awn offers money and closeness
then: Fir'awn says yes, and more: you will be {reward}of those brought near.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains it as: you will get {reward}more than you ask for{/reward}, I will make you my inner circle, those who sit with me. Minutes later, they would choose a different nearness.
now: The promotion that puts you in the boss's inner circle. The invite to the exclusive table. It feels like the top. {idea}But nearness to people with power is not the same as nearness to Allah.{/idea}
old: Getting close to powerful people is the best thing that can happen.
new: Being near the powerful is small next to being near Allah.
try: Notice one place where you chase someone's approval. Spend that energy on a dua instead.

title: Musa says: you go first. Throw.
subtitle: Calm confidence before the crowd
then: Musa tells them: {idea}throw what you are going to throw.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes Surah Ta Ha gives more detail, where they offered to go first or let him, and Musa said {idea}nay, you throw first.{/idea} He had been told earlier: We are with you, listening.
now: The other side presents first in the meeting. They have slides, data, confidence. You feel your stomach drop. {reward}You do not need to rush.{/reward} Let them show what they have, then bring what is true.
old: I have to strike first or I will lose.
new: When I trust Allah, I can let others go first and stay calm.
try: In your next discussion, let the other person finish fully before you speak.

title: By the might of Fir'awn, we will win.
subtitle: What they swore by before they threw
then: They threw their ropes and staffs and swore {trap}by the might of Fir'awn{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says this is how {trap}ignorant masses talk: this is by the virtue of so-and-so!{/trap} Surah Al-A'raf adds that they bewitched people's eyes and struck terror into them.
now: Before the big moment, what do you lean on? Your degree, your connections, my dad knows someone. {trap}It is easy to swear by a person.{/trap} {idea}Every might you lean on is borrowed from Allah's.{/idea}
old: My success comes from the people and power behind me.
new: All strength belongs to Allah. People are borrowing it.
try: Before your next important task, say la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

title: One staff swallowed every illusion they made.
subtitle: Truth does not argue with falsehood, it consumes it
then: Musa threw his staff and it {idea}swallowed up all that they falsely showed.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it caught them from every corner and {idea}did not leave any of them untouched.{/idea} He cites Al-A'raf: truth was confirmed, and all they did came to nothing.
now: Lies pile up: the rumor about you, the story someone spread, the version of events that is not true. It feels like a whole floor of snakes. {idea}One true thing, when it lands, can swallow all of them.{/idea}
old: There are so many lies against me that the truth cannot win.
new: One clear truth can swallow a hundred illusions.
try: If a lie is circulating about you, say the truth once, simply, to the person who matters.

title: The experts were the first to fall in prostration.
subtitle: Those who knew magic best saw the truth first
then: Minutes after asking about pay, the sorcerers {reward}fell down prostrate.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says they knew something their people did not: {idea}what Musa did could not be done by any human{/idea} unless Allah helped him. Their expertise is exactly what let them see it.
now: The doctor who has seen thousands of births and still says Subhan Allah. The engineer who understands the numbers and is still amazed. {idea}Knowing a field deeply can bring you closer to Allah, not further.{/idea}
old: The more I know about how things work, the less room there is for faith.
new: Real expertise can show you exactly where human power ends.
try: Think about something you understand well. Notice one part of it no human could have made.

title: We believe in the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: The magicians say the words Fir'awn mocked
then: Earlier Fir'awn had asked mockingly: {trap}and what is the Lord of the worlds?{/trap} Now his own magicians say it out loud: {idea}we believe in the Lord of the worlds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}the veil of disbelief had been lifted from their hearts.{/reward}
now: You have known someone for years who mocked religion at every dinner. Then one day they ask you quietly how to pray. {reward}Hearts can change in a moment.{/reward} Never assume the person across from you is finished.
old: People who are far from faith will always stay far.
new: A veil can lift in a single moment. Allah turns hearts.
try: Make dua today for one person you assume will never change.

title: The Lord of Musa and Harun. Not of Fir'awn.
subtitle: Naming exactly which Lord they meant
then: Fir'awn claimed to be lord of his people, so the magicians made it {idea}precise: the Lord of Musa and Harun.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they prostrated to Allah, {idea}Who sent Musa and Harun with the truth{/idea} and an obvious miracle. No one could twist their words.
now: At work you say you are not drinking for health reasons, or you skip the event without saying why. {idea}Sometimes being clear about why you do something is the brave part.{/idea} Saying it plainly, without drama, is enough.
old: It is safer to keep my faith vague in public.
new: Saying plainly whose way I follow can be a quiet act of courage.
try: Next time someone asks why you do a religious practice, give a short, honest answer.

title: You believed without my permission.
subtitle: A tyrant demands control over hearts
then: Fir'awn's first complaint is about permission. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}you should have asked me, for I am the ruler to be obeyed.{/trap} Then he accuses them of a plot with Musa, whom {idea}they had never met before that day{/idea}, and threatens them with cruel punishment.
now: Someone in your life wants a say over your heart. A partner who sulks when you start praying, a friend group that mocks you for changing. {idea}No one has to approve your faith before you live it.{/idea} Your heart answers to Allah.
old: I need the people around me to approve before I change.
new: My faith does not need anyone's permission but Allah's.
try: Do one act of worship today that you have been holding back because of what others think.

title: No harm. We are going back to our Lord.
subtitle: The magicians' answer to the threat
then: The threat only {reward}increased their faith{/reward}, Ibn Kathir says. They answered: {idea}no harm.{/idea} Our return is to Allah, Who will never let the reward of anyone who has done good be lost, and {reward}what you do to us is not hidden from Him.{/reward}
now: You lose the job for refusing to lie. A friendship ends because you would not join in. It hurts. {reward}But nothing done for Allah is lost.{/reward} You are going back to Someone who saw all of it.
old: If doing right costs me something, I have lost.
new: Nothing I give up for Allah is lost. He sees it and repays it.
try: Remember one thing you gave up for doing right. Tell Allah: I did it for You.

title: Forgive us. We were the first to believe.
subtitle: Hope at the very end of a life

row.title: our sins
sub: and the magic we were forced into

then: They hoped Allah would forgive {trap}the sins they committed and the magic Fir'awn forced them to do.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they were {reward}the first of the Egyptians to believe.{/reward} Their whole life of faith was a few minutes long, and it was full of hope.
now: You think it is too late. Too many years away, too many wrong turns. You will start when you are better. {reward}The magicians had minutes and they spent them hoping in Allah's forgiveness.{/reward} Start now.
old: I have done too much wrong for too long to be forgiven.
new: It is never too late to turn. Even minutes of faith are full of hope.
try: Ask Allah for forgiveness today in your own words, hopefully, not fearfully.

title: Leave at night. You will be followed.
subtitle: A command with the hard part included
then: After Musa stayed in Egypt a long time and the proof was established, Ibn Kathir says Allah told him to {idea}take the Children of Israel out by night{/idea}. Allah told him plainly: {trap}you will be pursued.{/trap} Musa did as he was commanded.
now: You are leaving the toxic job, the bad relationship, the old crowd. You know there will be messages, pressure, maybe anger. {idea}Knowing it will be hard is not a reason to stay.{/idea} Leave anyway, trusting the One who told you to go.
old: If leaving will bring trouble, maybe I should stay.
new: A right move can still come with trouble. That does not make it wrong.
try: Name one thing you know you need to leave. Write down the first small step.

title: Morning came, the quarters were empty, Fir'awn raged.
subtitle: Mobilizing every city to chase a few
then: Ibn Kathir says that the next morning, {trap}when there was nobody in the Israelite quarters{/trap}, Fir'awn grew angry, and his anger grew {idea}since Allah had decreed he was to be destroyed.{/idea} He sent callers to all his cities to bring his troops together.
now: Someone leaves your team, your group, your life, and you cannot let it go. You message everyone, rally people, chase. {trap}Anger at losing control can drive you somewhere you will regret.{/trap}
old: When someone leaves, I need to get control back.
new: Anger at losing control can push me straight into ruin.
try: When you feel the urge to chase someone who left, wait one day before acting.

title: They are just a small band.
subtitle: Shrinking people to justify crushing them
then: Fir'awn told his troops: {trap}these are but a small band{/trap}, meaning a small group. Ibn Kathir notes the Children of Israel were leaving with Musa, Harun and the believers. Fir'awn made them sound tiny so that {trap}chasing them sounded easy.{/trap}
now: You are one of three people at work who will not cut corners. One of two in the family who still pray. It feels small. {idea}Being few is not the same as being weak.{/idea}
old: If only a few people do what is right, it must not matter much.
new: Size does not decide who wins. Allah is with the few who are right.
try: Message one person who is quietly doing the right thing alone, and encourage them.

title: Everything about them enrages us.
subtitle: When someone's existence becomes an offense

row.title: enraged
sub: every time he hears of them

then: Fir'awn says {trap}they have done what has enraged us.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: every time we hear anything about them, it upsets us and makes us angry. Their crime was believing and leaving. {trap}The rage was his.{/trap}
now: There is someone whose posts you scroll past and feel your jaw tighten. They have done nothing to you. They just are. {idea}When someone simply existing makes you angry, the problem is often inside you.{/idea}
old: If someone always annoys me, they must be doing something wrong.
new: Constant anger at someone who does me no harm says more about my heart.
try: Think of someone who irritates you for no clear reason. Make a short dua for them.

title: We are many, ready, always on guard.
subtitle: The confidence of a cautious, armed crowd
then: Fir'awn says we are {trap}a host all assembled, amply forewarned.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains it as: we are constantly taking precautions. Some early scholars read it as his wish to {trap}destroy them to the last man.{/trap} He was then punished with the very thing he wanted to do to them.
now: You have the insurance, the backups, the security cameras, the plan B for everything. You feel untouchable. {idea}Preparation is good. But no plan protects you from Allah's decree.{/idea}
old: If I prepare for everything, nothing can go wrong.
new: Planning is wise, but my real safety is with Allah, not my precautions.
try: Before locking up tonight, say: I put my trust in Allah.

title: They rode out from gardens and springs, and never returned.
subtitle: Leaving every comfort behind to chase a grudge
then: Fir'awn thought he was choosing to chase. Allah says {idea}We expelled them{/idea} from gardens and springs. Ibn Kathir says they were {trap}thrown out of those blessings{/trap} and left behind gardens, rivers, wealth, provision and power.
now: You leave a good dinner with your family to answer a work email that could wait, or drive across town to win an argument. {trap}A grudge can make you walk out on every blessing you have.{/trap}
old: Settling this score is worth leaving everything else for.
new: Chasing a grudge can cost me every blessing I walked away from.
try: Today, choose to stay with something good instead of chasing something petty.

title: Treasures and honored places, all left behind.
subtitle: What status looks like on the way out
then: Along with gardens and springs they lost {reward}treasures and an honorable station.{/reward} Ibn Kathir lists what they left behind: {trap}wealth, provision, position and power{/trap} in this world. The whole government of Egypt rode out after the Israelites.
now: The corner office, the title on your email signature, the house in the right area. You worked hard for it, and it feels permanent. {idea}It is a trust, and it can change hands in a single morning.{/idea}
old: My position and wealth are mine for good.
new: Everything I have is on loan and can be handed to someone else.
try: Use one privilege you have today to make someone else's day easier.

title: The oppressed inherited what the oppressor left.
subtitle: How Allah turned the tables
then: Allah says {idea}thus{/idea}, and the Children of Israel inherited it. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse where Allah made {reward}the people who were considered weak{/reward} inherit the blessed lands, and the verse about wanting to do a favor to those who were weak in the land.
now: You are the junior one who gets talked over, the family member nobody listens to, the one with the smallest paycheck. {reward}Allah's way is not always the way of the strongest.{/reward} Be patient and do right.
old: People like me never end up on top.
new: Allah can lift the weak and let them inherit what the strong lost.
try: Encourage one person today who is often overlooked.

title: At sunrise, the army caught up.
subtitle: The whole government of Egypt in pursuit
then: Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn set out with {trap}a huge group: the leaders, ministers, nobles and soldiers{/trap}, the entire government of Egypt. They {trap}caught up with the Children of Israel at sunrise.{/trap} Allah had already told Musa they would be pursued.
now: You wake up and it is all hitting at once: the bills, the diagnosis, the email from HR. It feels like an army at sunrise. {idea}Allah knew this morning was coming before you did.{/idea}
old: When everything catches up with me at once, it is over.
new: The hardest morning can be the one right before Allah's help.
try: On your next hard morning, pray two units before reading any message.

title: Sea ahead, army behind. We are caught.
subtitle: The moment every exit looked closed
then: When the two groups saw each other, Musa's companions said {trap}we are sure to be overtaken.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains why: they were on the shore of the sea, with {trap}the sea ahead and Fir'awn's troops behind.{/trap} One of them asked Musa if this was really where Allah told him to bring them.
now: The rent is due, the account is empty, and the phone is ringing with a number you do not want to answer. Every road you can see is closed. {idea}What you can see is not everything there is.{/idea}
old: If I cannot see a way out, there is none.
new: Allah's way out is often the one I cannot see yet.
try: Write down your situation that feels like a dead end. Under it write: Allah sees a way.

title: No. My Lord is with me. He will guide me.
subtitle: Musa's certainty at the water's edge

row.title: No
sub: what you fear will not happen

then: Musa says {idea}no, my Lord is with me, He will guide me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: nothing you fear will happen to you, for {reward}Allah commanded me to bring you here, and He does not go back on His promise.{/reward} Musa did not yet know how. He knew Who.
now: You do not have the plan. You do not know how the bills will be paid or how the diagnosis ends. {reward}You can still say: my Lord is with me, He will guide me.{/reward} You do not need the whole map to take the next step.
old: I cannot feel calm until I know exactly how this works out.
new: I can be calm knowing Who is with me, even before I know how.
try: When panic rises today, say quietly: my Lord is with me, He will guide me.

title: Strike the sea. It splits into mountains of water.
subtitle: The way opens through the obstacle itself
then: As the army drew close, Allah told Musa to strike the sea, and {idea}it parted, each side like a huge mountain.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said it split into {reward}twelve paths, one for each tribe{/reward}, and Ibn Kathir says Allah made the sea bed dry. The thing blocking them became the road.
now: The illness that stops your career, the divorce that ends a whole life plan. It looks like the wall. {idea}Sometimes Allah opens a way straight through what is blocking you.{/idea} Do the small part in your hand, like Musa with his staff.
old: The obstacle in front of me is the end of the road.
new: Allah can turn the very obstacle into the path forward.
try: Do the one small action you can do about your problem today, and leave the rest to Allah.

title: The pursuers were drawn in after them.
subtitle: Following someone into a path not meant for you

row.title: the parted sea
sub: a path not meant for them

then: Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others said this means {idea}We brought Fir'awn and his troops near to the sea.{/idea} He saw the open path and followed. {trap}He thought he was the hunter{/trap}, while Allah was bringing him exactly where his story would end.
now: You see someone succeed by a path that worked for them, and you rush after it without asking if it is yours. Or you chase someone to prove a point. {trap}Pride makes you walk into places you should never enter.{/trap}
old: If a path is open, I can follow it wherever it goes.
new: Not every open road is meant for me. Pride can lead me where I should not go.
try: Before your next big decision, ask: am I doing this for Allah or to prove something?

title: Every one of them crossed safely.
subtitle: Not one of the believers was lost
then: Allah says He saved Musa and those with him {reward}all together.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains: We saved Musa and the Children of Israel and whoever followed their religion, {reward}and none of them were destroyed.{/reward} The same people who said we are caught all reached the other side.
now: The whole family got through the hard year. The team survived the layoffs. You were terrified, and then everyone made it. {reward}Remember that rescue.{/reward} Next time fear comes, bring that memory with you.
old: When things go well, it was probably luck.
new: The day everyone got through was Allah's rescue, and I should remember it.
try: Tell someone in your family about one time Allah got you all through something hard.

title: The same sea closed over the others.
subtitle: The end of Fir'awn and his army
then: Then Allah drowned the others. Ibn Kathir says {trap}Fir'awn and his troops were drowned and not one of them remained{/trap}. The whole government of Egypt that rode out that morning did not return. {idea}The same water that saved one group ended the other.{/idea}
now: The thing that rescues one person can ruin another: money, influence, a spotlight. It depends on what they do with it. {idea}Ask yourself which way your blessings are carrying you.{/idea}
old: Someone that powerful will always come out on top.
new: The same thing can save or ruin, depending on whose side I am on.
try: Pick one blessing you have, like money or influence, and use it today for something good.

title: A parted sea, and most still did not believe.
subtitle: The refrain after the story of Musa
then: The refrain returns after Musa's story. Ibn Kathir says this story, {idea}with its wonders and Allah's help to His believing servants{/idea}, is definitive proof of Allah's wisdom. A staff, a hand, a sea split in two. {trap}Yet most of them were not believers.{/trap}
now: You have seen your own parted seas: the recovery, the job that came at the last minute, the fight that ended in peace. {idea}How many more signs do you need?{/idea} The sign was never the problem.
old: If I had seen something like that, I would never doubt again.
new: Fir'awn saw the sea split. Signs do not make faith. The heart decides.
try: List three moments when Allah clearly helped you. Read the list when doubt comes.

title: Mighty with Fir'awn. Merciful with the magicians.
subtitle: Two names, two endings in one story
then: The second refrain closes Musa's story. Allah gave Fir'awn sign after sign and a long time in Egypt, and he refused. {idea}He is Mighty{/idea}: the army was ended in a moment. {reward}He is Merciful{/reward}: magicians who had served Fir'awn all their lives were welcomed in minutes.
now: You are somewhere between Fir'awn and the magicians right now. Maybe more stubborn than you want to admit. {reward}The magicians turned in a single afternoon.{/reward} The same Lord who is Mighty is waiting to be Merciful to you.
old: Either Allah is strict or He is forgiving. I am not sure which to expect.
new: He is both. His mercy is open to me today, before His might is needed.
try: Turn back to Allah today about one thing you have been stubborn about.

title: Now tell them the story of Ibrahim.
subtitle: The second story begins
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}commanded His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to recite this story{/idea} to his Ummah so they could follow Ibrahim's example: {reward}sincerity towards Allah, putting trust in Him, and worshipping Him alone.{/reward} Ibrahim had been guided from a very early age.
now: You are looking for a role model. You follow people online who show you how to dress, eat, earn. {reward}Ibrahim is offered as the example for how to trust and how to stand alone.{/reward} His story is meant to be lived, not just admired.
old: Prophets' stories are inspiring history, not a guide for my life.
new: Ibrahim's story is given to me as an example to actually follow.
try: As you read the next verses, pick one thing Ibrahim does and copy it this week.

title: He starts at home: what do you worship?
subtitle: Ibrahim questions his father and his people
then: Ibrahim's first move is a question to {idea}his father and his people{/idea}: what do you worship? Ibn Kathir paraphrases it as: what are these statues to which you are so devoted? {idea}He begins by asking, not attacking.{/idea}
now: Your family spends hours on things you think are empty. You could lecture them. Ibrahim asked a question. {idea}What do you get out of this? What are we really living for?{/idea} A good question can open more than a speech.
old: To change my family, I need to tell them they are wrong.
new: A sincere question can reach further than a lecture.
try: Ask someone close to you one honest question about what matters most to them.

title: We worship idols, and we stay devoted to them.
subtitle: Proud devotion to something empty
then: They answered proudly: {trap}we worship idols, and to them we are ever devoted.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: we are devoted to worshipping them and praying to them. They were sincere, committed, faithful. {idea}Just to the wrong thing.{/idea}
now: You check the stock app forty times a day. You never miss the gym, the match, the series. You are deeply devoted. {idea}Devotion is not the question. What you are devoted to is.{/idea}
old: Being committed and consistent is what makes something good.
new: Devotion is only as good as what it is given to.
try: Check your screen time today. Ask honestly what you are most devoted to.

title: Do they even hear you when you call?
subtitle: Ibrahim's first test for any god
then: Ibrahim asks: {idea}do they hear you when you call?{/idea} The question is simple. Ibn Kathir notes that {trap}they knew their idols could not do anything.{/trap} A god who cannot hear you is not a god.
now: At 2 a.m. in the hospital waiting room, who do you call? Your bank balance does not hear you. Your follower count does not. {idea}Allah hears the call you whisper with no sound at all.{/idea}
old: The things I rely on will be there for me when I need them.
new: Only Allah truly hears me when I call in the dark.
try: Tonight, call on Allah in your own language about one need, even silently.

title: Can they help you? Can they even hurt you?
subtitle: Ibrahim's second test: real power
then: Ibrahim continues: {idea}do they benefit you, or do they cause harm?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the people {trap}knew their idols could not do anything.{/trap} A thing that cannot help or harm cannot deserve worship.
now: You are afraid of what people will say, as if their opinion could ruin you. You chase approval as if it could save you. {idea}Ask Ibrahim's question: can it really help me? Can it really hurt me?{/idea}
old: What people think of me has the power to make or break me.
new: Only Allah can truly benefit or harm me. Everything else is borrowed.
try: Name one fear of people's opinion. Ask yourself: can they really harm me without Allah's will?

title: Our fathers did it. That is the whole argument.
subtitle: Tradition as a replacement for thinking
then: They could not say the idols hear or help. So they said {trap}we found our fathers doing so.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: they knew their idols could do nothing, but {trap}they had seen their fathers doing this, so they made haste to follow{/trap} in their footsteps.
now: At the wedding, the family insists on the expensive custom no one can afford. At work, it is just how it has always been done. {trap}That is how we have always done it is not a reason.{/trap} Keep the good of your elders, and check the rest.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: Tradition is worth keeping when it is true, not just because it is old.
try: Pick one habit you do only because your family always did. Ask if it pleases Allah.

title: Have you really looked at what you worship?
subtitle: Ibrahim asks them to see clearly
then: After their answer about their fathers, Ibrahim says: {idea}then do you see what you have been worshipping?{/idea} He asks them to really look at the statues. Ibn Kathir says he was challenging them: if these idols {trap}have any influence, let them harm me.{/trap}
now: You have lived years on autopilot around something: a habit, a goal, a person you put above everything. {idea}Ibrahim's question is simple: have you actually looked at it?{/idea} Stop for a second and see it for what it is.
old: I know what I live for. I do not need to examine it.
new: Looking honestly at what I give my life to is the first step.
try: Take two minutes tonight and write what you spent most of your energy on this week.

title: You, and your fathers from long ago.
subtitle: Old does not mean true

row.title: nothing
sub: an old mistake is still a mistake

then: Ibrahim widens the question: {idea}you and your ancient fathers.{/idea} They had said we found our fathers doing this. He answers that the age of the practice does not change what the idols are. {trap}A thing that never heard anyone did not start hearing because many people prayed to it.{/trap}
now: The family feud that started three generations ago. The way the men in your family talk to their wives because their fathers did. {trap}Something being old does not make it right.{/trap} You can be the one who stops it.
old: Something done for generations must have a good reason behind it.
new: An old mistake repeated for generations is still a mistake.
try: Name one pattern from your family you do not want to pass on. Do one thing differently today.

title: They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: Ibrahim's open, fearless break with idols
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim's words: {trap}if these idols have any influence, let them do me harm{/trap}, for I am their enemy and do not care about them. He compares it to Nuh and Hud saying {idea}plot against me, all of you{/idea}, and to Ibrahim asking how he could fear what they associate with Allah.
now: You are afraid that if you stop the lucky charm, skip the horoscope, or say no to the habit, something bad will happen. {idea}They have no power to harm you.{/idea} Only Allah does, and you are with Him.
old: If I cut off this thing I depend on, something bad might happen to me.
new: Nothing besides Allah can harm me, so I can let go without fear.
try: Let go of one superstition or false comfort today, and say: I rely on Allah.

title: He made me, and He shows me the way.
subtitle: The first reason Ibrahim worships Allah
then: Ibrahim says he will worship only the One who does these things. First: {idea}who created me, and it is He who guides me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says He is the Creator who has decreed things and {reward}guides His creation{/reward} to them.
now: You are lost about the career, the move, who to marry. You read every article and ask every friend. {idea}The One who made you knows how you work.{/idea} Ask Him for guidance before you ask the internet.
old: Finding my path is entirely up to me.
new: The One who made me is the One who guides me.
try: Before your next decision, pray two units and ask Allah to guide you.

title: He is the one who feeds me and gives me water.
subtitle: Every meal traced back to its source
then: Second reason: {reward}He feeds me and gives me drink.{/reward} Ibn Kathir describes how Allah {idea}drives the clouds and sends down water{/idea}, reviving the earth and bringing out fruits, and sends water fresh and sweet for people and animals to drink.
now: You grab a sandwich between meetings and drink from a plastic bottle without looking at it. You think your paycheck bought it. {idea}Your paycheck is just the last step of a long chain that starts with rain.{/idea}
old: I feed myself with the money I earn.
new: Allah feeds me. My job is one of the ways He sends it.
try: Before your next meal, say Bismillah slowly and think of the rain that made it.

title: When I fall sick, He is the one who heals me.
subtitle: Ibrahim's careful words about illness
then: Ibrahim says {idea}when I am ill{/idea}, not when He makes me ill. Ibn Kathir says he attributed sickness to himself {idea}out of respect towards Allah{/idea}, and that no one can heal except Him, {reward}who heals with the means that lead to recovery.{/reward}
now: You are in the clinic waiting room with the prescription in your hand. Take the medicine, follow the doctor. {reward}And know who is actually doing the healing.{/reward} The pills are the means. The cure is from Him.
old: If I recover, it is because of the medicine.
new: I use the medicine, and I know it is Allah who heals through it.
try: The next time you take medicine, say: O Allah, You are the Healer.

title: He will cause me to die, then bring me back.
subtitle: Life and death in the same hands
then: Ibrahim says: {idea}who will cause me to die, and then bring me to life.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains He alone gives life and causes death, {reward}for He is the One who originates and repeats.{/reward} No idol could do either.
now: You get the call about a friend your age. Suddenly the deadline at work does not matter. {idea}Death is in His hands, and so is what comes after.{/idea} That thought can be heavy. It can also be the calmest thing you know.
old: Death is something to avoid thinking about.
new: The same Lord who gives me life will bring me back after death.
try: Spend one minute today thinking about death calmly, then do one good deed.

title: Even Ibrahim said: I hope He forgives me.
subtitle: Hope, not certainty, from the Friend of Allah
then: After listing what Allah does for him, Ibrahim says {reward}who I hope will forgive me my faults{/reward} on the Day of Recompense. Ibn Kathir says {idea}no one can forgive sins in this world or the next except Him.{/idea} The Close Friend of Allah still speaks with hope, not certainty.
now: You compare yourself to others: at least I pray, at least I do not do what they do. {idea}Ibrahim, the leader of the believers, said I hope.{/idea} Humility and hope belong together.
old: I am doing better than most people, so I am fine.
new: Even the best of people hoped for forgiveness. I should hope humbly too.
try: Tonight ask Allah's forgiveness for something you think is small.

title: Give me wisdom, and put me with good people.
subtitle: Ibrahim's first request for himself
then: Having described Allah, Ibrahim begins to ask. First, {reward}Hukm{/reward}, which Ibn Abbas said means knowledge. Then {reward}join me with the righteous{/reward} in this world and the next. Ibn Kathir links it to the Prophet ﷺ saying, as he was dying, O Allah, with the Exalted Companion.
now: Look at your list of duas. A bigger house, a better job, a spouse. Fine. {idea}Ibrahim's first request was knowledge and good company.{/idea} The people you sit with shape who you become.
old: My duas should mostly be about getting what I need in life.
new: Knowledge and good companions are among the best things to ask for.
try: Add one line to your dua today: O Allah, put me with the righteous.

title: Let me be remembered well by those who come after.
subtitle: Asking for a good legacy
then: Ibrahim asks for {reward}an honorable mention in later generations.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains: cause me to be remembered well after my death, so {reward}I will be taken as a good example.{/reward} Allah granted it: peace be upon Ibrahim is said to this day.
now: What will your kids say about you when you are gone? Your coworkers, your neighbors? {idea}Not a viral post. The way you treated people.{/idea} That is the legacy that lasts.
old: Caring about how I am remembered is vanity.
new: Asking to be remembered as a good example is a prayer Ibrahim made.
try: Do one thing today you would want your children to remember you for.

title: Make me one who inherits the Garden of Delight.
subtitle: The aim beyond the good name
then: Ibrahim asks to be {reward}one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains the pairing: {idea}bless me in this world with a good name after I am gone{/idea}, and in the Hereafter with the Garden.
now: You plan the pension, the savings, the five-year career goals. Good. {idea}Do you have a plan for the Garden too?{/idea} Ibrahim asked for it by name. You can too.
old: Paradise is something that will work itself out somehow.
new: Paradise is worth asking for directly and planning for.
try: Ask Allah today, by name, for Jannat al-Firdaws.

title: And forgive my father. He has gone astray.
subtitle: A son's love for a father who opposed him
then: Ibrahim prays: {reward}forgive my father, he is of the erring.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes it was because of {idea}a promise he had made to him{/idea}, citing the verse in At-Tawbah, and that Ibrahim later stopped this when it became clear. That verse calls Ibrahim tender-hearted and forbearing.
now: Your father does not share your faith, or mocks the way you live. Some days you are angry. {idea}You can disagree deeply and still care, still hope, still be kind.{/idea} Ibrahim's love for his father did not disappear.
old: If my parent opposes my faith, I should cut off my care for them.
new: I can stand firm in my faith and still be a tender-hearted child.
try: Do one kind thing for a parent today, whatever your differences.

title: Do not shame me on the Day everyone is raised.
subtitle: Asking to be spared disgrace before all creation
then: Ibrahim asks: {idea}disgrace me not on the Day they are resurrected.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}protect me from shame{/reward} on the Day when all creatures, the first and the last, will be raised. He also reports from Al-Bukhari that Ibrahim will meet his father on that Day.
now: You would do anything to avoid embarrassment at work or in front of in-laws. You rehearse what to say, delete old posts. {idea}There is a Day when everyone will be there at once.{/idea} That is the shame worth preparing against.
old: What matters most is what people think of me now.
new: The shame I most need protection from is on the Day all are raised.
try: Quietly fix one hidden thing today you would not want seen on that Day.

title: The Day money and children cannot help.
subtitle: Everything people lean on, set down
then: Ibn Kathir explains that a man's wealth {trap}will not protect him{/trap}, even if he paid a ransom of an earthful of gold, nor his sons, even if he offered all people on earth. {idea}Only faith in Allah and sincere devotion to Him{/idea} will be of use that Day.
now: You work overtime to give your kids everything, and you tell yourself it is all for them. Good. {idea}But on that Day, they cannot carry you, and your account balance cannot either.{/idea} Invest in the one thing that crosses.
old: Providing for my family is enough to make me safe.
new: My family and money are blessings, not my ticket on that Day.
try: Give a small amount in charity today with the intention it is for that Day.

title: Only a sound heart gets through.
subtitle: The one thing worth bringing to Allah
then: Except {reward}one who comes to Allah with a sound heart{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this means free from impurity and shirk. Ibn Sirin said the clean heart {idea}knows Allah is true and the Hour will come.{/idea} Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said it is the healthy heart, the opposite of a diseased one.
now: You track your steps, your sleep, your cholesterol. You know your heart rate. {idea}When did you last check the health of your inner heart?{/idea} The grudges, the envy, the quiet doubts. That is the heart you take with you.
old: As long as my actions look good, my heart does not matter much.
new: What I bring to Allah in the end is my heart. Its health is everything.
try: Let go of one grudge today. Clean one corner of your heart.

title: Paradise is brought close to those who were mindful.
subtitle: The Garden comes to meet its people

row.title: those who strove
sub: and chose it over this world

then: Ibn Kathir says Paradise {reward}will be brought close to its people, adorned and decorated{/reward} for them to see. Its people are {idea}the pious who preferred it to whatever was in this world{/idea} and worked for it here.
now: You chose the dawn prayer over sleep, honesty over the easy lie, patience over the angry message. Nobody noticed. {reward}On that Day, the Garden comes to meet the one who made those choices.{/reward}
old: My small sacrifices go unnoticed and do not count for much.
new: Every time I choose Allah over this world, I am walking toward a Garden coming to meet me.
try: Make one small choice today for the next life over this one, and tell no one.

title: The Fire is brought into view of the astray.
subtitle: The other side of the same Day
then: Ibrahim's description of the Day continues. Right after the Garden comes the other scene: {trap}the Fire placed in full view of the astray.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says it will be shown to them and their hearts will reach their throats. {idea}One verse for each road.{/idea}
now: You know which way you are drifting. The habit you keep promising to quit, the prayer you keep pushing back. {idea}The road you walk now is the scene you will see then.{/idea} The good news is that you can still turn the wheel today.
old: The Hereafter is far away. I will think about it later.
new: The direction I walk today is the direction I am facing that Day.
try: Pick one drift in your life and take one step back toward Allah today.

title: Where are the things you used to worship?
subtitle: The question that echoes Ibrahim's
then: Ibrahim asked his people {idea}what do you worship?{/idea} On the Day, the same question comes back as a rebuke: {trap}where are those you used to worship?{/trap} Ibn Kathir says it will be said to them by way of reproach.
now: Think of what you put first when you are scared: the savings, the connections, the reputation. {idea}Picture the moment they are all gone.{/idea} Where are they? What is left is what you turned to Allah with.
old: The things I rely on will be there when it really matters.
new: Only Allah is there in every moment. Everything else disappears.
try: Name one thing you lean on more than Allah. Say a dua handing that worry to Him.

title: Can they help you? Can they even help themselves?
subtitle: False gods cannot even save themselves
then: Ibrahim had asked: do they benefit you or harm? The same test is now asked again: {trap}can they help you or help themselves?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that the gods worshipped instead of Allah {trap}cannot help you today, and cannot even protect themselves.{/trap}
now: The influencer whose advice you followed, the trend you built your life around, the person you were afraid to disappoint. {idea}Ask Ibrahim's question now, while it is still a question.{/idea} Can this help me? Can it even help itself?
old: The people and things I follow are strong enough to carry me.
new: If something cannot save itself, it cannot save me.
try: Unfollow or mute one account that pulls you away from Allah.

title: Thrown in together, the misled and those who misled.
subtitle: Followers and leaders share one end
then: Mujahid said this means {trap}they will be hurled into it.{/trap} Others said they will be thrown on top of one another, {trap}the disbelievers and their leaders who called them to shirk.{/trap} The ones who followed and the ones who led share one end.
now: You went along with the office gossip because everyone did. You shared the post because a friend did. {idea}Following does not erase your part.{/idea} Each of us answers for where we chose to walk.
old: If I only followed others, the blame is on them.
new: I am responsible for whom I choose to follow.
try: Before sharing or joining something today, ask: would I stand by this alone?

title: And all of Iblis's soldiers with them.
subtitle: The ones who whispered share the end
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}all of the hosts of Iblis{/trap} will be thrown in together with them. The whisperers who made idol worship look attractive do not escape. {idea}Those who serve Iblis end up where Iblis ends.{/idea}
now: The thought at midnight: just one more video, one more look, one more lie to cover it. It feels like your own voice. {idea}Some whispers are recruitment.{/idea} You do not have to join that army.
old: The urges I have are just my own personality.
new: Some whispers come from Iblis. I can refuse them and seek refuge.
try: When a bad urge comes today, say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim and move.

title: Even there, they argue with each other.
subtitle: Blame-shifting continues after it is too late
then: They dispute with each other inside it. Ibn Kathir says {trap}the weak will say to their arrogant leaders: we were following you, can you help us?{/trap} He cites Surah Sad: the mutual dispute of the people of the Fire is the very truth.
now: The group project fails and everyone's first move is the blame thread. The family plan falls apart, and the arguing starts. {idea}Blame is easy. Taking responsibility while it can still change something is the real work.{/idea}
old: When things go wrong, finding who is to blame is what matters.
new: Blaming others later changes nothing. Owning my part now does.
try: In your next mistake with others, say first: this part was mine.

title: By Allah, we were clearly wrong.
subtitle: The confession that came too late
then: Ibn Kathir says that after blaming their leaders, {idea}they will realize they themselves are to blame.{/idea} They swear: {trap}by Allah, we were truly in manifest error.{/trap} The error was clear. They saw it only when it could no longer be fixed.
now: You know there is something you are wrong about. You have known for a while. Your pride says keep going. {idea}Saying I was wrong today costs a little pride. Saying it later costs much more.{/idea}
old: Admitting I am wrong is humiliating, so I will hold out.
new: Admitting I was wrong now is a mercy. Later, it is only regret.
try: Tell one person today: I was wrong about that.

title: We made you equal to the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: Naming the real mistake
then: Their confession names the exact error: {trap}we held you as equals with the Lord of the worlds.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}we obeyed your commands as we should have obeyed the commands of the Lord{/trap}, and worshipped you along with Him.
now: You would never bow to your boss. But when he says to lie on the report, you do it, against what Allah asks. {idea}Obeying someone over Allah is a quiet way of making them equal to Him.{/idea}
old: As long as I do not literally worship something, I am fine.
new: Putting someone's orders above Allah's is a way of equalling them with Him.
try: Notice one place you obey a person over Allah. Choose Allah there once.

title: It was the wrongdoers who led us astray.
subtitle: Who you let lead you
then: They say {trap}none has brought us into error except the criminals.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: nobody called us to this except the evildoers. They had Ibrahim calling them to Allah too. {idea}They chose which voice to follow.{/idea}
now: There are two voices in your life. The friend who pulls you to the masjid and the friend who pulls you to the club. The mentor who says be honest, the one who says everyone cuts corners. {idea}You are choosing which one leads you.{/idea}
old: I just ended up with the people I ended up with.
new: I choose who leads me. That choice shapes where I end up.
try: Spend time this week with one person who brings you closer to Allah.

title: Now we have no one to speak for us.
subtitle: Every expected intercessor gone
then: They say: {trap}now we have no intercessors.{/trap} Ibn Kathir compares it to the verse where they ask: are there any intercessors for us, or could we be sent back to do other than what we did? {trap}Those they hoped would speak for them are gone.{/trap}
