now: You always had someone to get you out of trouble. The uncle with connections, the friend in HR, the lawyer cousin. {idea}There is a Day when that system ends.{/idea} What speaks for you then is what you did with Allah.
old: There will always be someone to get me out of trouble.
new: The connections I count on here will not work there. My deeds will.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that only Allah will see.

title: And not a single close friend.
subtitle: When even friendship cannot reach
then: Then they add: {trap}nor a close friend.{/trap} The leaders they followed and the companions they kept now argue with them. The friendships built around worshipping others besides Allah {trap}offer nothing{/trap} on that Day.
now: Your phone is full of friends: the group chats, the weekend crew. Ask which of them would remind you of Allah if you drifted. {reward}Friendship built on Allah is the kind that still holds.{/reward}
old: Any close friend is a good friend.
new: The friends who bring me nearer to Allah are the ones who last.
try: Message one friend today and remind them of something good, gently.

title: If only we could go back and believe.
subtitle: The wish that cannot be granted
then: They wish {trap}if only we had a chance to return, we would be believers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Allah knows that if they were sent back they would return to what was forbidden. {idea}The return they wish for is the life they already had.{/idea}
now: You are holding the thing they wished for: a today. Breath, time, a chance to change. {reward}You are already back.{/reward} Every morning you wake up is the second chance someone on that Day will beg for.
old: I will change someday when life settles down.
new: Today is the second chance. I am already living it.
try: Start one good thing today that you have been saving for later.

title: Ibrahim's arguments were a sign. Most still refused.
subtitle: The refrain after the story of Ibrahim
then: After Musa, the sign was a split sea. After Ibrahim, the refrain returns for a different kind of sign. Ibn Kathir says {idea}in the dispute of Ibrahim with his people and his proof of Tawhid there is a sign{/idea}, clear evidence that there is no god but Allah. {trap}Yet most were not believers.{/trap}
now: You do not need a miracle to believe. Ibrahim used questions anyone can ask: does it hear me, can it help me, who feeds me? {idea}Answer those honestly about your own life.{/idea} That is the sign.
old: I would believe more firmly if I saw a miracle.
new: Ibrahim's plain questions are signs. I can ask them myself today.
try: Ask yourself Ibrahim's questions about one thing you rely on, and answer honestly.

title: Mighty over the idols. Merciful to Ibrahim's hope.
subtitle: The two names after the scenes of the Day

row.title: the Merciful
sub: the one who hopes is heard

then: The second refrain closes Ibrahim's story, right after the scene of regret. {idea}He is the Mighty{/idea}: what was worshipped besides Him cannot help even itself. {reward}He is the Merciful{/reward}: Ibrahim said I hope He forgives me, and the door to that hope is open now.
now: You just read about people who wished they could come back. You are here. {reward}Your Lord is Merciful today.{/reward} Pray Ibrahim's prayer for a sound heart while you still can.
old: After reading about the Fire, I mostly feel afraid.
new: The same Lord is Mighty and Merciful. Today, His mercy is open to me.
try: Say Ibrahim's dua today: do not disgrace me on the Day they are raised.

title: Deny one messenger, and you deny them all.
subtitle: The third story begins: Nuh
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh was {idea}the first Messenger sent to the people of earth after they started to worship idols.{/idea} They denied only Nuh, yet Allah says they denied the messengers, because {trap}disbelieving in him was like disbelieving in all{/trap} the Messengers.
now: You keep the parts of the faith you like and ignore the one that is inconvenient. The prayer yes, the honesty in business maybe not. {idea}It is one message from one Lord.{/idea} Picking and choosing is a quiet kind of denial.
old: I can accept the parts of the message that fit my life.
new: The message is one whole. Rejecting part of it touches all of it.
try: Pick one teaching you have been ignoring and act on it once today.

title: Their brother asked: will you not fear Allah?
subtitle: A warning from one of their own
then: Allah calls Nuh {reward}their brother{/reward}. He was one of them. His first words are a question: {idea}will you not have taqwa?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it as: do you not fear Allah when you worship others instead of Him?
now: The warning that annoys you most often comes from your own sibling, your own friend, your own spouse. {reward}They say it because they are your people.{/reward} A brother's warning is love speaking.
old: When family criticizes me, it is because they do not understand me.
new: Sometimes the warning comes from family because they care the most.
try: Think of a sincere warning from someone close. Thank them for it.

title: I am a messenger you can trust.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing taken away
then: Nuh says {idea}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I convey the messages of my Lord {reward}and I do not add anything to them or take anything away.{/reward} His trust was in passing it on exactly.
now: Someone tells you a secret, a colleague asks you to pass a message, a friend shares a hadith in the group. {idea}Do you pass it on exactly, or add a little spin?{/idea} Being trustworthy is in the small relays too.
old: A little exaggeration when I pass something on is harmless.
new: Trust means passing things on exactly as they were given to me.
try: Next time you repeat what someone said, say it exactly, without adding anything.

title: Fear Allah, and follow me.
subtitle: Taqwa first, then following
then: Nuh puts it in order: {idea}have taqwa of Allah{/idea}, then obey me. He is not asking for a following of his own. Ibn Kathir says he is {reward}faithfully fulfilling the mission{/reward} Allah gave him, so following him means following Allah's message.
now: You follow a speaker online, a sheikh, a teacher you love. Good. {idea}Ask what the order is: do you follow them because they bring you to Allah, or for them?{/idea} Taqwa comes first.
old: Following a good teacher is enough on its own.
new: I follow teachers because they lead me to Allah. Allah comes first.
try: Next time you listen to a lesson, ask: what does Allah want me to do with this?

title: I am not asking you for anything.
subtitle: Advice with no price tag

row.title: what is in it for him?

then: Nuh says {idea}no reward do I ask of you for it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I do not want any payment for the advice I give you; {reward}I will save my reward for it with Allah.{/reward} He had nothing to gain from them.
now: You help a friend move, check a cousin's CV, teach your neighbor's kid to read. You catch yourself waiting for thanks. {reward}Do it for Allah, and you will never be disappointed.{/reward} The pay comes from Him.
old: If I help someone, I deserve at least some thanks back.
new: When I help for Allah, my reward is already safe with Him.
try: Help someone today and do not mention it to anyone.

title: So fear Allah and obey me. He says it again.
subtitle: Repeating the call, with a new reason
then: Nuh repeats the same line. The first time it followed his trustworthiness. Now it follows the fact that he asks for nothing. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}it is clear to you that I am telling the truth{/idea}, so fear Allah. {reward}He kept calling, with patience.{/reward}
now: You told your teenager once and gave up. You reminded your spouse gently once and stopped. {reward}Nuh repeated himself, gently, giving a new reason each time.{/reward} Some good things need to be said more than once.
old: If I said it once and it did not work, there is no point repeating it.
new: Patient, kind repetition is part of caring for someone.
try: Gently repeat one piece of good advice to someone you love, in a new way.

title: Believe you? Your followers are the lowest of us.
subtitle: Rejecting truth because of who accepted it
then: The leaders of Nuh's people said: we will not follow you and {trap}become equal to the meanest people{/trap} who follow you. Ibn Kathir notes they called them the lowest among us. The Prophet ﷺ heard the same from Quraysh: {trap}your followers are slaves and the poor.{/trap}
now: You skip the small masjid because the people there are not your type. You ignore good advice because it came from the cleaner, or the intern. {idea}The truth does not change with the clothes of the one who carries it.{/idea}
old: If the people accepting it are not impressive, it probably is not worth much.
new: The truth is true no matter who accepts it first.
try: Sit with or listen to someone today whom you would usually overlook.

title: What do I know about what they used to do?
subtitle: Not checking backgrounds at the door
then: Ibn Kathir explains Nuh's reply: {idea}what does it have to do with me if they follow me?{/idea} No matter what they did before, {reward}I do not have to check on them and examine their background.{/reward} All he had to do was accept them if they believed.
now: A brother with a prison record starts coming to the masjid. A new convert with tattoos joins the circle. People whisper about their past. {reward}Their past is not yours to investigate.{/reward} Welcome them.
old: Before I accept someone, I should know what they have done.
new: If someone turns to Allah, their past is not my business to dig into.
try: Greet one newcomer at your masjid or community warmly this week.

title: Their account is with my Lord, not with me.
subtitle: Leaving hearts to the One who knows them

row.title: mine
sub: I can tell who is sincere

then: Nuh continues: {idea}their account is only with my Lord, if you could but know.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}whatever is in their hearts is for Allah to know.{/reward} Nuh's task was the message, not judging the inner state of those who accepted it.
now: You decide someone's hijab is for show, someone's charity is for likes, someone's tears in prayer are fake. {idea}You cannot see inside them.{/idea} Their account is with Allah. Yours is too.
old: I can usually tell when someone's religion is fake.
new: Only Allah knows what is in a heart. I will leave the account to Him.
try: Catch one judgment about someone's sincerity today and let it go.

title: I will not push away the believers.
subtitle: Refusing to trade the poor for the powerful
then: Ibn Kathir says it seems the leaders {trap}asked him to drive these people away, and then they would follow him.{/trap} Nuh refused: {reward}I am not going to drive away the believers.{/reward} Whoever believes in me belongs to me and I to him, noble or common.
now: Your group wants to look good. Someone suggests not inviting the awkward guy so the important people come. {reward}Nuh would not trade one sincere person for a room full of the influential.{/reward}
old: It is worth leaving some people out to attract more important ones.
new: I will not push away sincere people to please the powerful.
try: Include someone in your next gathering who usually gets left out.

title: I am only a clear warner.
subtitle: Knowing the limits of your role
then: Nuh closes his answer: {idea}I am only a plain warner.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I have been sent as a warner, and {reward}whoever believes in me belongs to me{/reward}, whether upper-class or lower-class. He does not decide who deserves the message.
now: You run the youth group, the study circle, the family WhatsApp. It is easy to start choosing who belongs. {idea}Your job is to share what is good, clearly and to everyone.{/idea} Not to guard the door.
old: Part of my role is deciding who deserves to hear this.
new: My role is to share clearly. Who accepts it is not mine to sort.
try: Share one good reminder today with someone you would not usually share it with.

title: Stop, Nuh, or we will stone you.
subtitle: After years of calling, a death threat
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh {idea}stayed among his people a long time, calling them night and day, in secret and openly.{/idea} The more he called, the more they clung to disbelief. In the end they said: {trap}if you do not stop, we will stone you.{/trap}
now: You have been patient for years with a family member, a difficult coworker, a friend. It only got worse. {idea}Sometimes your patience is not failing. You did your part, like Nuh.{/idea} Their hardness is theirs.
old: If they only got worse, I must have done it wrong.
new: I can call with patience for years and still not be the cause of their refusal.
try: Tell Allah about one long effort that has not worked. Ask Him for strength.

title: My Lord, my people have called me a liar.
subtitle: Bringing the pain straight to Allah
then: When the threat came, Nuh turned to Allah: {idea}My Lord, my people have denied me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Allah responded to his prayer, and compares it to another verse where Nuh says {trap}I have been overcome, so help me.{/trap}
now: You were not believed. The family took the other side, the manager did not back you. You want to post about it, call everyone. {idea}Nuh took it to his Lord first.{/idea} Tell Him exactly what happened.
old: When I am hurt, I need everyone to know what they did.
new: My deepest complaints are best brought to Allah first.
try: Next time you feel wronged, pray and tell Allah before telling anyone else.

title: Judge between us, and save me and the believers.
subtitle: Handing the outcome to Allah
then: Nuh asks Allah to {idea}judge between me and them with a decisive judgement{/idea}, and to {reward}save me and the believers with me.{/reward} He did not take matters into his own hands. He asked Allah to decide, and remembered those who believed with him.
now: There is a conflict you cannot resolve, with an ex, a business partner, a sibling. You fantasize about getting even. {idea}Hand it to Allah: judge between us.{/idea} And remember to pray for the people on your side.
old: If I do not settle this myself, it will never be fair.
new: I can hand the judgment to Allah and ask Him to protect the good people with me.
try: Make a dua for justice in one conflict, and include the people who stood by you.

title: Saved in a ship packed full.
subtitle: Nuh and those with him are rescued
then: Allah says {reward}We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says the laden ship was {idea}filled with cargo and the couples, one pair from every species.{/idea} The followers the elite called the lowest were the ones on board.
now: The people others looked down on, the quiet family next door, the ones who did not make it to the top of the company. {reward}Allah's rescue is not sorted by status.{/reward} Be with the believers, whoever they are.
old: The safe place is with the popular and powerful.
new: Safety is with the believers, however lowly others think they are.
try: Make a dua today for one humble believer you know.

title: Then the rest were drowned.
subtitle: The end of those who refused Nuh
then: Allah says {trap}then We drowned the rest thereafter.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: We saved Nuh and all who followed him, and drowned all those who disbelieved in him and went against his commands. {idea}For years the door was open. Then the ship sailed.{/idea}
now: You keep saying you will fix it later: the prayer, the apology, the debt you owe. {idea}Every door that is open now will close one day.{/idea} The ship is still at the dock. Get on.
old: There will always be more time to turn back.
new: The chance is open now, but not forever. Today is the day to board.
try: Do the one thing today you keep telling yourself you will do later.

title: A whole flood, and still most did not believe.
subtitle: Nuh's story ends with a sign few accepted

row.title: proof forces belief
sub: show me and I will follow

row.title: a sign invites
sub: most still choose to look away

then: Nuh called his people for a very long time, in secret and openly. They answered with a threat to stone him. He asked Allah to judge between them, and {reward}he and the believers were saved in the laden ship{/reward} while the rest drowned. Then comes the line: {idea}in that is a sign.{/idea}
now: You have seen it happen. A friend survives a crash, a scare at the hospital, a near loss of everything. For a week they pray and call their mother. Then life returns to normal and the lesson fades. {trap}The sign was clear. The change did not last.{/trap}
old: If I saw something truly clear, I would change for good.
new: Signs are already everywhere; what is rare is a heart that keeps responding to them.
try: Think of one moment this year that shook you. Write down what it was trying to teach you.

title: Mighty enough to end it, merciful enough to wait.
subtitle: Two names closing the story of Nuh
then: Nuh's people had years of his calling before anything happened. When the end came, {idea}it was total for those who refused{/idea} and {reward}complete safety for those in the ship.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ, grieving over Makkah's rejection, hears the same two names after each story.
now: You keep a habit you know is wrong, and nothing bad has happened yet. It is easy to read that quiet as approval. {reward}The quiet is a door held open.{/reward} The same Lord who waits is also able.
old: Since nothing has happened to me, it must not matter much.
new: His patience with me is mercy, and His might means the patience is not forever.
try: Pick one thing you have been delaying to fix with Allah. Take the first small step today.

title: Denying one messenger is denying them all.
subtitle: The people of 'Ad enter the story
then: After Nuh's people came 'Ad, living in the curved sand-hills of the Ahqaf near Yemen. They were tall, strong, and richly provided for. Allah sent one of their own, Hud, to them. The verse says {trap}they denied the messengers{/trap}, plural, because {idea}every messenger carried the same call.{/idea}
now: Your father warned you about something years ago. Then a teacher said it. Then a friend. Then a stranger online. You dismissed each one separately. {idea}It was one message wearing different faces.{/idea}
old: I am only disagreeing with this one person.
new: When the same truth keeps reaching me through different people, I am answering the truth, not the person.
try: Notice one piece of advice you have heard from more than one person. Give it a fair hearing today.

title: Their brother asked: will you not be mindful?
subtitle: Hud speaks as family, not as a stranger
then: Allah sent Hud, {idea}one of their own{/idea}, to 'Ad. He opened with the same words Nuh had used with his people: a question, not a shout. {reward}Will you not have taqwa?{/reward}
now: Your cousin is sliding into something harmful. You could post a long lecture in the family group chat. Or you could sit next to him and ask one honest question. {idea}Hud chose the question.{/idea}
old: To correct someone I need to be firm and tell them they are wrong.
new: The best warning sounds like a brother asking, not a judge announcing.
try: If you need to advise someone today, start with a question instead of a statement.

title: He was a messenger they could trust.
subtitle: Hud points to his own honesty
then: Hud tells 'Ad that he is {reward}a trustworthy messenger{/reward} to them. He was one of their own, so they knew his character. The Quraysh too knew the Prophet ﷺ well, {trap}yet called him a poet and a sorcerer.{/trap}
now: A colleague who has never lied to you raises a concern about a deal everyone else loves. You brush it off because it is inconvenient. {idea}Their track record was the reason to listen.{/idea}
old: I decide whether to listen based on whether I like what I hear.
new: When someone honest brings a hard truth, their honesty is part of the evidence.
try: Think of the most honest person in your life. Ask them one thing they think you should hear.

title: Be mindful of Allah, then follow the guide.
subtitle: The order matters: Allah first, then His messenger
then: Hud's call is short: {idea}worship your Lord and obey your Messenger.{/idea} He does not ask them to follow him for himself. Obeying him is simply how mindfulness of Allah takes shape in daily life.
now: You say you fear Allah, but when guidance gets specific, about your tongue, your money, your prayer times, you start negotiating. {trap}Taqwa that never becomes action stays a feeling.{/trap}
old: As long as I respect God in my heart, the details are optional.
new: Mindfulness of Allah shows itself in following the guidance He sent.
try: Choose one specific piece of guidance you already know and follow it fully today.

title: He wanted nothing from them.
subtitle: No fee, no favor, only from the Lord

row.title: what is in it for him

then: Hud says the same line Nuh said before him: {reward}my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.{/reward} A messenger who asks for nothing has {idea}no reason to mislead.{/idea}
now: You help your neighbor move, then quietly wait for the thank-you post, or a favor later. When it does not come, you feel cheated. {reward}Hud's reward was already booked elsewhere.{/reward}
old: If I give my time, I should get something back from people.
new: Good done for Allah is already paid; people's thanks is a bonus, not the wage.
try: Do one helpful thing today and tell no one about it.

title: Monuments on every hill, built just to show off.
subtitle: Building for amusement, not for need

row.title: wasted lives
sub: time and bodies spent on nothing

then: 'Ad built a huge, dazzling structure at each well-known crossroads. {trap}Not because they needed it, but for fun and to show off their strength.{/trap} Hud objected because it {idea}wasted time, exhausted people's bodies, and benefited no one{/idea} in this world or the next.
now: The car you financed so it would look good in the driveway. The renovation planned mostly for photos. Weekends spent on projects whose real purpose is to be seen. {idea}What is it actually for?{/idea}
old: If I can afford it, building something impressive is my business.
new: Effort spent only to be admired is effort lost, and other people often pay for it.
try: Look at one thing you are working on. Ask honestly who it is really for.

title: Building fortresses as if they would never leave.
subtitle: Strong walls do not make a person last
then: Mujahid explained these as {trap}fortresses built strong and high, structures meant to last.{/trap} They built as though they would stay forever. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}it would not happen; they would cease, like those before them.{/idea}
now: You plan the next thirty years in detail: mortgage, retirement, the house extension. You have never once planned for the day you leave all of it. {idea}The walls will outlast you.{/idea}
old: If I build a secure enough life, I will be safe.
new: Nothing I build keeps me here; I should build for where I am going too.
try: Next to one long-term plan you have, write one plan for your akhirah.

title: When they struck, they struck like tyrants.
subtitle: Strength without mercy

row.title: how do I use it
sub: when I have the upper hand

then: Ibn Kathir describes 'Ad as {trap}strong, violent and tyrannical.{/trap} When they seized someone, they did it with no limit and no mercy. Their strength was a gift, but {idea}they turned it against people.{/idea}
now: You are the manager now. A junior makes a mistake in front of the client. You could correct them quietly, or crush them in the meeting. {idea}Power shows who you are.{/idea}
old: When I am in the right and in charge, being harsh is fair.
new: Having the upper hand is exactly when I am tested on mercy.
try: Next time you have power over someone today, a child, a worker, a waiter, choose the softer word.

title: After naming their wrongs, he asked again.
subtitle: Hud repeats his call after the warning
then: Hud has just named three things: {trap}building for show, building as if to live forever, and striking like tyrants.{/trap} Then he does not condemn them. He repeats his invitation: {idea}worship your Lord and obey your Messenger.{/idea}
now: Your friend lays out, honestly, what you have been doing wrong. The list stings. But they end with: and I know you can change. {idea}A real warning always ends with a way back.{/idea}
old: Once my faults are named, there is no point trying.
new: Naming my faults is how the invitation to return becomes specific.
try: Take one fault someone pointed out to you recently. Treat it as a direction, not a verdict.

title: Fear the One who gave you what you know.
subtitle: Hud turns from warning to reminding of gifts
then: Hud begins {reward}reminding them of the blessings Allah had given them.{/reward} He does not need to list unknown things. He points to {idea}what they already know{/idea}, what they see every day.
now: Your salary, your health, the fact that your kids woke up today. You know all of these. You have just stopped seeing them as given. {reward}You already know the list.{/reward}
old: What I have came from my own effort.
new: Everything I know I have was supplied to me, and the Giver deserves my mindfulness.
try: Before you sleep, name five things you have today that you did not create.

title: Livestock and children were His gifts.
subtitle: Wealth and family named as provision
then: Hud names the two things 'Ad valued most: {reward}their animals and their sons.{/reward} Wealth and family were their pride and their power. He reminds them that {idea}Allah is the one who aided them with both.{/idea}
now: Your child's graduation photo. Your savings slowly growing. You feel proud, and it is natural. {idea}Pride can still say: You gave me this.{/idea}
old: My family and my wealth are what I built.
new: My family and my wealth are gifts I am trusted with, not trophies I earned alone.
try: Thank Allah out loud today for one person in your family, by name.

title: Gardens and springs in the middle of sand.
subtitle: The land itself was a gift
then: 'Ad lived among sand-hills near Hadramawt, yet Ibn Kathir notes they had {reward}gardens, rivers, crops and fruits.{/reward} Hud completes the list of gifts with {idea}gardens and springs{/idea}, things they saw every day.
now: You turn on the tap and water comes out. Clean, warm if you want. You complain when the pressure is low. {reward}Somewhere today, someone walked an hour for less.{/reward}
old: Running water and green spaces are just normal.
new: What feels normal to me is provision someone else is praying for.
try: The next time you drink water today, pause and say alhamdulillah before the first sip.

title: I fear for you, said the brother.
subtitle: A warning that comes from care
then: Hud ends: {idea}I fear for you{/idea} the punishment of a great day, if you disbelieve and oppose. Ibn Kathir says he called them with {reward}words of encouragement and words of warning{/reward}, but it was to no avail.
now: Your mother keeps calling about the late nights and the skipped meals. It feels like nagging. {idea}It is fear for you, said in the only way she knows.{/idea}
old: People who warn me are trying to control me.
new: A warning can be the most loving thing someone says to me.
try: Call or message someone who has warned you about something. Thank them for caring.

title: Preach or do not, it makes no difference to us.
subtitle: 'Ad close the door on advice
then: After Hud warned, encouraged and clearly explained, 'Ad replied: {trap}it is the same to us whether you preach or not.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains it as {trap}we will not give up our ways.{/trap} This consoled the Prophet ﷺ: the problem was not his message.
now: Your sister says, gently, that you seem unhappy at that job. You answer: I know, I know. You have said I know for three years. {idea}Hearing is not the same as letting it in.{/idea}
old: I have heard all this advice before, so it does not apply to me anymore.
new: The day advice makes no difference to me is the day I should worry most.
try: Pick one piece of advice you keep shrugging off. Sit with it for five quiet minutes.

title: This is only the way of the ancients.
subtitle: Dismissing truth as old stories or old habits
then: Scholars read their words two ways. Some: {trap}what you bring is only tales of the ancients{/trap}, the same thing Quraysh said about the Quran. Others: {trap}we follow the religion of our fathers{/trap}, we live as they lived and die as they died, with no resurrection.
now: Someone questions a habit in your family: the way money is handled, the way anger is shouted out. Your answer comes fast: this is how we have always done it. {idea}Always is not a reason.{/idea}
old: If my parents and grandparents did it, it must be fine.
new: What I inherited still has to be weighed against the truth.
try: Name one family habit you have never questioned. Ask yourself if it is actually good.

title: We are not going to be punished.
subtitle: The calm certainty of the careless
then: Following their forefathers, 'Ad believed {trap}there would be no resurrection and no judgement.{/trap} So they concluded, {trap}we are not going to be punished.{/trap} Their confidence rested on nothing but their own wish.
now: The test results are waiting in your inbox. You have not opened them for a week. As long as you do not look, you feel fine. {idea}Not looking does not change the result.{/idea}
old: Things will probably be fine for me in the end.
new: My sense of safety is not a guarantee; only turning to Allah is.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding looking at, a bill, a message, a habit, and face it.

title: The strongest people met something stronger.
subtitle: The end of 'Ad and the sign in it
then: 'Ad kept denying, so Allah destroyed them with a fierce, cold wind. Ibn Kathir notes it {idea}suited their nature{/idea}: they boasted of being the strongest, so they were overpowered by something stronger. {trap}Their mountain fortresses did not help them at all.{/trap}
now: You think your job title, your savings, your health insurance make you untouchable. Then one phone call from a doctor changes everything in a minute. {idea}Every strength I have is borrowed.{/idea}
old: I have built enough security that nothing can really shake me.
new: The strength I trust most is the one that can be overpowered fastest.
try: Name the strength you lean on most. Thank Allah for it, and ask Him not to let you rely on it instead of Him.

title: Mightier than 'Ad, merciful to those who listened.
subtitle: The refrain after Hud's story
then: 'Ad asked, who is mightier than us? The answer comes here: {idea}your Lord is the Almighty.{/idea} Yet before anything happened, {reward}He sent them one of their own{/reward}, who reminded them of cattle, children, gardens and springs.
now: You are proud of how capable you are, how much you can handle. Then you remember all the warnings you got before your last big mistake: the friend, the feeling, the near-miss. {reward}Each one was mercy.{/reward}
old: I am strong enough to handle my own life.
new: Only Allah is truly mighty, and the warnings I get are His mercy reaching me first.
try: Recall one warning you received before a past mistake. Thank Allah for it, even late.

title: Thamud denied the messengers too.
subtitle: A new people, the same pattern
then: Thamud were Arabs living in {idea}Al-Hijr, between Wadi Al-Qura and Greater Syria.{/idea} They came after 'Ad and before Ibrahim. Salih called them to worship Allah alone, but {trap}they refused, rejecting and opposing him.{/trap}
now: Your older friend went through the same debt spiral you are entering now. You watched it happen. You still tell yourself your case is different. {idea}History is a warning only if you read it.{/idea}
old: What happened to others does not really apply to me.
new: Other people's stories are lessons sent ahead to me.
try: Think of someone's past mistake you saw up close. Check whether you are walking toward it.

title: Salih asked his people the same gentle question.
subtitle: A new brother, the same words
then: Salih, {idea}their brother{/idea}, opens exactly as Nuh and Hud did: {reward}will you not have taqwa?{/reward} The same words in each story showed the Prophet ﷺ that his call was the call of every messenger before him.
now: You keep looking for some new, clever spiritual advice. A new app, a new podcast, a new method. The answer is often the oldest one: {idea}be mindful of Allah.{/idea}
old: I need something new and different to change my life.
new: The oldest advice is usually the one I have not really tried.
try: Skip the new content today. Do one old simple thing: pray on time with full attention.

title: Salih too was known to be trustworthy.
subtitle: Character comes before the message
then: Salih says {reward}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/reward} He lived among Thamud, so his honesty was known. Every messenger in this surah says it, because {idea}a trusted life is the ground a message stands on.{/idea}
now: You want your kids to pray. You want your coworkers to take your faith seriously. But they watch whether you keep your word about small things first. {idea}Trust is built before it is used.{/idea}
old: What I say matters more than how I live.
new: My honesty in small things is what gives my words weight.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you said it, on time.

title: Mind Allah, and follow the one He sent.
subtitle: Salih's call in two parts
then: Salih called Thamud {idea}to worship Allah alone, with no partner{/idea}, and to {idea}obey whatever commands were conveyed to them.{/idea} But they refused, rejecting and opposing him.
now: You believe in Allah without question. But when you are told to lower your gaze, hold your tongue, or pay what you owe, you suddenly have questions. {trap}Belief that skips the commands is half a step.{/trap}
old: I believe, and that is what really counts.
new: Belief shows its truth when I follow what I was told.
try: Pick one clear command you find hard. Follow it once today, just for Allah.

title: No fee for the truth.
subtitle: Salih's reward was with Allah
then: Salih told Thamud {reward}he did not seek any reward from them{/reward}, only from Allah. Then {idea}he reminded them of Allah's blessings.{/idea} His call cost them nothing and asked nothing for himself.
now: A friend gives you honest advice about your marriage. They gain nothing from it, and they risk the friendship by saying it. {idea}That is how you know it is sincere.{/idea}
old: Everyone who tells me what to do has an angle.
new: Advice that costs the giver and gains them nothing deserves my respect.
try: Give someone one piece of honest, kind advice today, expecting nothing back.

title: Do you think you will be left here, secure?
subtitle: The comfortable life is not permanent
then: Salih warned Thamud that {trap}Allah's punishment could overtake them{/trap}, while reminding them that {reward}Allah had given them ample provision and safety from all kinds of danger.{/reward} His question: do you think this will just go on?
now: A stable job, a good neighborhood, health that has never failed you. It starts to feel like the way things simply are. {idea}Will you be left in it, secure?{/idea}
old: My comfortable life is just how things are.
new: Every day of safety is a gift on loan, and a test of what I do with it.
try: Thank Allah today for one kind of safety you usually never notice.

title: Gardens and springs, given again.
subtitle: Thamud had the same gifts as 'Ad
then: Like Hud before him, Salih pointed to {reward}gardens and flowing springs.{/reward} Thamud had been given the same kind of blessings 'Ad had, and {trap}'Ad's end was known to them.{/trap}
now: You get the promotion your friend got before you, the one that pulled him away from his family. Same gift, same test. {idea}Will you handle it differently?{/idea}
old: Blessings are just rewards to enjoy.
new: When I receive what others had before me, I also receive their test.
try: Think of a blessing you share with someone who struggled with it. Ask Allah to help you carry it well.

title: Fields of crops and palms heavy with soft fruit.
subtitle: Abundance described up close
then: Salih names their crops and {reward}date palms with soft clusters.{/reward} Ibn Abbas explained it as {reward}ripe and rich{/reward}, or growing luxuriantly. Salih did not speak of blessings vaguely; he pointed at the fruit on their trees.
now: The bowl of fruit on your kitchen counter. The bread from the bakery down the road. You eat it while scrolling, not tasting. {idea}Gratitude starts with noticing specifics.{/idea}
old: I am grateful in general.
new: Real gratitude names the exact thing in front of me.
try: At your next meal, name three specific foods on the plate and thank Allah for each.

title: Skilled hands carving homes into mountains.
subtitle: Talent spent on extravagance
then: Thamud {reward}hewed houses out of the mountains with great skill{/reward}, still visible today. Ibn Kathir joins the two meanings: they were skilled, but {trap}they built them as extravagant play, with no need for them as dwellings.{/trap}
now: You are talented with code, design, cooking, or words. Yet most of that talent goes into things that only impress people or kill time. {idea}Skill is a gift with a purpose.{/idea}
old: My talent is mine to use however I like.
new: The skill in my hands was given, and I will be asked what I built with it.
try: Use your best skill today for something that helps someone, even for twenty minutes.

title: With all this given, mind the Giver.
subtitle: Salih's call after listing their blessings
then: Ibn Kathir explains Salih's words as: {idea}pay attention to what benefits you in this world and the next.{/idea} Worship the Lord who created you and {reward}gave you provision so you could worship Him alone and glorify Him morning and evening.{/reward}
now: Payday arrives. You plan the shopping, the bills, the treat for yourself. You do not plan a single minute of thanks. {idea}The provision came with a purpose.{/idea}
old: My blessings are mine to enjoy; worship is a separate thing.
new: Provision is given so I can turn to the Provider, morning and evening.
try: Say a short dhikr this morning and this evening, both, just to mark the day with Him.

title: Do not follow those who go beyond limits.
subtitle: Choosing whose orders you take
then: Salih warns Thamud not to obey {trap}the extravagant{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says these were {trap}their chiefs and leaders, who called them to shirk, disbelief and opposition to the truth.{/trap} The people had to choose whose command to follow.
now: The loudest people in your office, your friend group, your feed, set the tone. You start laughing at what they laugh at and wanting what they want. {idea}Whose orders are you really following?{/idea}
old: Everyone important is going this way, so it must be right.
new: Status does not make someone worth obeying; truth does.
try: Notice one opinion you picked up just from someone popular. Decide if you actually agree.

title: They spoil the land and never set it right.
subtitle: The mark of leaders not to follow
then: Salih describes the leaders of Thamud: {trap}they make mischief in the land, and reform not.{/trap} The test of whom to follow is simple: {idea}do they leave things better or worse?{/idea}
now: In your home, you are a leader too. After you walk in the door each evening, is the house calmer or tenser? After you join a conversation, is it kinder or crueler? {idea}What do you leave behind?{/idea}
old: Only people in power can spoil or fix the world.
new: Every one of us either spreads harm or sets things right in our small corner.
try: Fix one small thing today that you usually leave broken: a strained message, a mess, a tone.

title: You must be bewitched, they told him.
subtitle: Labeling the messenger instead of answering
then: When Salih called them to worship their Lord, Thamud said {trap}you are only of those bewitched.{/trap} Mujahid said they meant {trap}one affected by witchcraft.{/trap} Quraysh said similar things about the Prophet ﷺ. {idea}A label is easier than an answer.{/idea}
now: Someone at work points out a real problem with your plan. Instead of looking at it, you say: they are just jealous, they are always negative. {idea}The label saves you from the question.{/idea}
old: If someone criticizing me has something wrong with them, I can ignore them.
new: Labeling the speaker does not answer what they said.
try: Next time you want to dismiss someone with a label, respond to their actual point instead.

title: You are just a man like us. Show a sign.
subtitle: Why him and not us?
then: Thamud asked, {trap}how can you receive revelation when we do not?{/trap} Then they pointed to a rock and demanded a she-camel from it. Salih made them promise to believe, and prayed. The rock split and the camel came out. {trap}Some believed, but most disbelieved.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself: if I just got a clear answer to my prayer, I would be consistent. Then the job comes through, the scan is clear, and a month later your prayers are back to rushed. {idea}The sign was not the missing piece.{/idea}
old: If I got one clear sign, I would never doubt again.
new: Signs do not fix a heart that has decided not to follow.
try: Recall one prayer Allah answered for you. Do one act today to honor it.

title: One day for her water, one day for yours.
subtitle: The sign came with a simple rule
then: Salih said the camel would {idea}drink from their water one day, and they the next.{/idea} She stayed among them a long time, grazing, and {reward}they drank her milk until every one had his fill.{/reward} The sign was also a daily test of sharing.
now: Your shared office kitchen, the family car, the one bathroom in the morning. Taking turns sounds small. {idea}A lot of faith is kept or lost in how we share.{/idea}
old: Taking my full share of everything is just fair.
new: Keeping a limit Allah set, even an inconvenient one, is part of the sign.
try: Give up your turn at something today, a seat, a slot, a portion, without being asked.

title: Do not touch her with harm.
subtitle: One clear limit, one clear warning
then: Salih {trap}warned them of Allah's punishment if they did her any harm.{/trap} The rule was simple and clear. The camel was not only an animal; {idea}she was the sign they themselves had asked for.{/idea}
now: There is one clear line you know Allah has drawn in your life. You tell yourself it is small, that crossing it once does not matter. {idea}Clear lines are clear for a reason.{/idea}
old: Small limits do not really matter.
new: A limit from Allah is never small, because of Who set it.
try: Name one clear limit you keep testing. Stay fully on the right side of it today.

title: They killed her, and woke up regretful.
subtitle: Regret that came too late
then: The camel lived among them for a long time and fed them. Then, {trap}as the time of their destruction drew near, they conspired to kill her.{/trap} The verse says {trap}they became regretful{/trap}, but the deed was already done.
now: The message you sent in anger at midnight. The words you cannot take back from the argument. In the morning, the regret is real. {idea}The pause before is worth more than the regret after.{/idea}
old: I can always fix it afterward.
new: Some things cannot be undone, so the time to stop is before.
try: Next time you feel the urge to act in anger today, wait ten minutes first.

title: They asked for a sign, then destroyed it.
subtitle: The sign after Thamud's story
then: After killing the camel, Thamud were {trap}overtaken by events they were not expecting.{/trap} An earthquake and a mighty shout came upon them. Then the refrain: {idea}in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.{/idea} They had seen the exact sign they demanded.
now: You asked Allah for a way out of the debt, the bad relationship, the habit. The way out came. Then you walked back in. {idea}The sign was given; the question is what you did with it.{/idea}
old: I would act differently if only I had clear proof.
new: Often the proof has come, and I am the one who let it go.
try: Think of one way out Allah opened for you. Check that you have not walked back in.

title: Mercy gave them milk, might answered their defiance.
subtitle: The two names after Salih's story
then: The camel stayed among Thamud {reward}for a long time, and they drank their fill of her milk.{/reward} That was mercy, every single day. Only when they killed her did they meet {idea}the All-Mighty.{/idea}
now: Think of how many mornings you have been given since you first knew you needed to change. Each one came with breakfast, health, a chance. {reward}That long stretch of ordinary days is mercy.{/reward}
old: Allah's might is something to be afraid of from a distance.
new: His mercy runs long before His might acts, and I am living inside that mercy now.
try: Use today's ordinary morning for one change you have been putting off.

title: The people of Lut denied the messengers.
subtitle: A new nation in Ibrahim's lifetime
then: Lut, {idea}the nephew of Ibrahim{/idea}, was sent to a mighty nation in Sadum (Sodom) during Ibrahim's lifetime. He called them to worship Allah alone and obey the messenger. He also forbade {trap}a sin they had invented that was unknown before their time.{/trap}
now: Every person has a sin that has become normal for them. It does not feel like rebellion anymore; it feels like just how things are. {idea}The story starts by asking you to see your own.{/idea}
old: Denial is something other people do.
new: Any part of me that refuses the call is denying the same messengers.
try: Quietly name one wrong you have stopped calling wrong. Ask Allah to help you see it clearly.

title: Lut asked as a brother: will you not be mindful?
subtitle: He lived among them and called them family
then: Lut came from Ibrahim's family, yet the Quran calls him {idea}their brother.{/idea} He lived among them and opened, like Nuh, Hud and Salih, with {reward}will you not have taqwa?{/reward}
now: Your cousin is doing something you know is wrong. It is easy to talk about him behind his back in the family chat. {idea}It is harder, and better, to talk to him as a brother.{/idea}
old: When people do wrong, I distance myself and judge.
new: The messengers called people back as brothers, not from a distance.
try: Pray by name for one person whose choices worry you.

title: A trustworthy messenger in an untrustworthy town.
subtitle: Lut's honesty stood out
then: Lut tells them {reward}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/reward} He delivered the message as Allah gave it, even though he was one man against a mighty nation. Ibn Kathir notes he was sent {idea}to call them to Allah alone.{/idea}
now: Everyone at your job cuts the same small corners: padded hours, borrowed supplies, little lies to the client. Staying honest makes you the odd one. {idea}That is exactly when it counts.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me does it, my honesty does not change anything.
new: Being trustworthy matters most where it is rare.
try: Refuse one small dishonest shortcut today that everyone else takes.

title: Fear Allah, and follow His messenger.
subtitle: Lut's call, same as every brother before
then: Before forbidding their sin, Lut calls them to {idea}worship Allah alone and obey the messenger Allah sent.{/idea} Every messenger in this surah starts here. The specific wrongs are named after the heart is addressed.
now: You keep trying to quit a habit by willpower alone, and keep falling back. Maybe the start is not the habit. {idea}Maybe it is how present Allah is in your day.{/idea}
old: I need to fix my behavior before I can get close to Allah.
new: Getting closer to Allah is what gives me the strength to fix my behavior.
try: Before facing a habit you struggle with today, spend two minutes in dua about it.

title: Lut asked nothing for himself.
subtitle: The fourth messenger with the same words
then: Lut repeats what each messenger said: {reward}my reward is only from the Lord of all that exists.{/reward} He later faced threats of expulsion for his message. {idea}He had nothing to gain from them and much to lose.{/idea}
now: You speak up about something wrong in your community, knowing it may cost you friends or invitations. You do it anyway, for Allah. {reward}That reward is held safe.{/reward}
old: If speaking the truth costs me, it is not worth it.
new: What I lose for speaking truth, Allah repays from His side.
try: Say one true and kind thing today that you have been holding back out of fear.

title: Lut named the sin they had invented.
subtitle: Crossing a limit no one had crossed before

row.title: they invented it
sub: and made it the town's way

then: Lut {trap}forbade them from the sin they had invented, unknown on earth before their time{/trap}, and taught them to turn to {reward}the wives Allah had created for them.{/reward} The verse asks them to see what they had made normal.
now: This story is not a weapon to point at others. It asks you a quiet question: {idea}where have you turned away from what is lawful and good for you{/idea}, toward something you know crosses Allah's line?
old: Once a whole society accepts something, it stops being a question.
new: Allah's limits do not move just because a crowd moves past them.
try: Thank Allah today for one lawful good He gave you, and protect it.

title: Leaving what your Lord made for you.
subtitle: Transgression is walking past the lawful
then: Lut {idea}taught them to turn to the wives Allah had created for them.{/idea} The lawful was already provided and close at hand. He calls them {trap}a trespassing people{/trap}: they went past what was given to reach what was forbidden.
now: Your spouse is in the next room while you scroll toward something you should not. Your salary is enough, and you still reach for what is not yours. {idea}The lawful was already provided.{/idea}
old: I cross limits because what is allowed does not satisfy me.
new: Allah already placed what is good for me within reach; transgressing is walking past it.
try: Spend real attention today on one lawful blessing you usually overlook, like your spouse or your family.

title: Stop, Lut, or we will drive you out.
subtitle: When people want to be clean, the town expels them
then: Their response was only: {trap}if you do not give up what you have brought, we will expel you from among us.{/trap} Elsewhere they said, {idea}they are people who want to be clean and pure.{/idea} His purity was their complaint.
now: You stop joining the gossip at work, or stop drinking at the team dinner. Slowly, the invitations stop. {idea}Sometimes being left out is a sign you are on the right side.{/idea}
old: If people push me out, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Being pushed out for doing right is a cost the messengers paid too.
try: If you have lost a circle for doing right, thank Allah for the reason, and seek better company.

title: I detest what you do.
subtitle: Lut declares himself free of their deed
then: When Lut saw {trap}they would not give up their ways{/trap}, he said he was among those who detest {idea}their deed.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}I do not like it, I do not accept it, I have nothing to do with it.{/idea}
now: Your friends joke about something cruel, and you laugh along so you do not seem uptight. Silence and laughter both sound like approval. {idea}You can refuse the deed without hating the person.{/idea}
old: If I stay friendly, I have to accept what they do.
new: I can stay kind to people while clearly refusing their wrong.
try: Next time a cruel joke comes up today, do not laugh. Calmly change the subject.

title: My Lord, save me and my family.
subtitle: A prayer for protection from surrounding harm
then: After declaring himself free of their deed, Lut {idea}prayed to Allah{/idea}: save me and my family from what they do. He was one man with his household, surrounded by a whole town. {reward}He turned the problem over to his Lord.{/reward}
now: You worry about what your kids see on their phones, at school, in the street. You cannot control all of it. {idea}You can make Lut's dua for them every night.{/idea}
old: Protecting my family depends entirely on me.
new: I do my part, and I ask the One who can actually protect them.
try: Tonight, make dua by name for each person in your household to be kept safe from harm.

title: So We saved him and his family.
subtitle: The dua was answered
then: Allah answered: {reward}We saved him and his family.{/reward} Allah commanded him to leave with his family at night and {idea}not to turn around{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}they patiently obeyed the command of Allah and persevered.{/reward}
now: You need to leave something behind: a job that pulls you into wrong, a circle that drags you down. Leaving is the first step. {idea}Not turning back to it is the second.{/idea}
old: Once I pray, the rescue should just happen to me.
new: Rescue often comes as a command to walk out, and patience not to look back.
try: If there is something you have already left for Allah, take one step today to not go back to it.

title: Except one who stayed behind, his own wife.
subtitle: Being close to a prophet was not enough
then: Ibn Kathir says this was {trap}his wife, who was a bad old woman{/trap}. She stayed behind and met the fate of those who remained. She lived inside a prophet's house, and {idea}it did not save her.{/idea}
now: Your father is the imam, your mother never misses a prayer, your brother memorized the Quran. It is easy to feel covered by them. {idea}Their closeness to Allah is theirs.{/idea}
old: Coming from a religious family keeps me safe.
new: No one's faith can carry me; I have to choose my own.
try: Do one act of worship today purely as your own, not because family expects it.

title: Then the rest were destroyed.
subtitle: After the believers left
then: The word {idea}then{/idea} matters. Lut and his family were brought out first. {trap}Afterward, the others were destroyed.{/trap} Allah separated those who obeyed from those who stayed.
now: When things fall apart around you, a company scandal, a friend group collapsing, it can feel random. {idea}The question is where you were standing before it came.{/idea}
old: When disaster comes, it does not matter what I did.
new: What I choose before the test decides where I stand in it.
try: Ask yourself honestly where you are standing today. Take one step to the side you want to be on.

title: A rain on those who had been warned.
subtitle: The weight is in the word warned
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}rained upon them stones of baked clay, piled up.{/trap} The verse names them by one quality: {idea}those who had been warned.{/idea} Lut had told them plainly, and they had threatened him in return.
now: The doctor told you about your blood sugar. Your boss told you about the deadlines. Your heart told you about that habit. {idea}You were warned. That is a mercy while there is still time.{/idea}
old: Bad outcomes just come out of nowhere.
new: Most warnings come early; what I do with them is mine.
try: Take one warning you have been given, health, money or faith, and act on it today.

title: A sign left in the land itself.
subtitle: The refrain after Lut's story
then: Ibn Kathir notes the land of Lut's people became a lake {idea}well known in the land of Al-Ghur, the Jordan Valley.{/idea} Travelers passed it. The refrain repeats: {trap}in this is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.{/trap}
now: You drive past the hospital, the cemetery, the house of the neighbor who lost everything. You have seen it so often it means nothing now. {idea}A sign can become scenery.{/idea}
old: I have seen enough reminders to know them already.
new: The danger is not missing the sign, but getting used to it.
try: Next time you pass a place that reminds you of death or loss, stop for a moment and reflect.

title: Mighty against the town, merciful to one family.
subtitle: Both names seen in Lut's story
then: A mighty nation was ended, and one small family walked out at night. {idea}His might was not stopped by their numbers.{/idea} {reward}His mercy found the few who obeyed.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ and his small group in Makkah heard this.
now: You feel outnumbered: the only one in your office who prays, the only one in your family trying to change. {reward}Allah's mercy does not need a crowd.{/reward}
old: If most people are doing it, I am probably safe going along.
new: Allah sees the one who obeys, even alone among many.
try: Do one right thing today that you would normally skip because no one around you does it.

title: The people of the thicket denied too.
subtitle: Madyan, named after what they worshipped
then: The companions of Al-Aykah were, by the most correct view, {idea}the people of Madyan.{/idea} They took their name from Al-Aykah, {trap}a tree, or a thicket of tangled trees, which they used to worship.{/trap} They too denied the messengers.
now: People are often known by what they chase: the gym guy, the crypto guy, the one always talking about her career. {idea}What would you be named after?{/idea}
old: What I am obsessed with is just a hobby.
new: What I give my heart to can become my identity.
try: Ask a close friend what you talk about most. Listen to the answer honestly.

title: Shu'ayb spoke, but not called their brother.
subtitle: A missing word that tells a story

row.title: their name
sub: tied to the tree they worshipped

row.title: he was not one of them
the name was the tree's
sub: he shared their blood, not that

then: Here the Quran says {idea}when Shu'ayb said to them{/idea}, not their brother Shu'ayb. Ibn Kathir explains it is because {trap}their name denoted their worship of Al-Aykah.{/trap} Shu'ayb was their brother by blood but had no share in that name.
now: You can belong to a family, a team, a culture, and still not share in what is wrong in it. {idea}Belonging does not mean taking the whole label.{/idea}
old: If I belong to a group, I have to carry everything it stands for.
new: I can be loyal to my people without sharing in what they worship besides Allah.
try: Think of one thing your circle takes for granted that you do not agree with. Keep your distance from it, kindly.

title: A trustworthy messenger to a dishonest market.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's honesty set against their cheating
then: Shu'ayb says {reward}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes he {idea}commanded them to be fair in weights and measures.{/idea} A people who cheated in trade were sent a man defined by trust.
now: You sell a used phone and do not mention the cracked camera. You file an expense that is a bit rounded up. {idea}Trustworthiness is tested at the till, not only at the mosque.{/idea}
old: Business is business; faith is separate.
new: Being trustworthy covers my receipts as much as my prayers.
try: In your next sale or purchase, mention one detail that is in the other person's favor.

title: Fear Allah and obey me, said the fifth messenger.
subtitle: The same call reaches Madyan
then: Shu'ayb gives the same call as Nuh, Hud, Salih and Lut: {idea}have taqwa of Allah, and obey me.{/idea} For Madyan, obeying him would mean {reward}fair weights and measures{/reward}, right where they made their living.
now: Your shop, your freelance invoices, your online store. That is where your taqwa will be tested most this week. {idea}Mindfulness of Allah goes to work with you.{/idea}
old: I am mindful of Allah when I pray.
new: Mindfulness of Allah is just as real when I quote a price.
try: Before your next work task today, say bismillah and remember Allah is watching the work.

title: To traders, he asked no payment.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's call came free
then: To a people who lived by buying and selling, Shu'ayb said: {reward}no reward do I ask of you for it; my reward is only from the Lord of all the worlds.{/reward} He was the {idea}fifth messenger in this surah to say it.{/idea}
now: You are used to paying for everything: courses, coaching, advice. Then someone gives you honest guidance for free and you value it less. {idea}Free does not mean cheap.{/idea}
old: Advice I did not pay for cannot be worth much.
new: The most valuable guidance often comes from people asking nothing in return.
try: Thank someone today who once gave you good advice for free.

title: Give as you take, take as you give.
subtitle: Full measure, no loss to others
then: Shu'ayb commanded them to give full measure. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do not cause loss by giving short measure while taking full measure when you are the ones taking.{/trap} {idea}Give as you take, and take as you give.{/idea}
now: You count your change carefully at the shop. But when you split the restaurant bill, you round your share down. When you bill a client, you round up. {idea}One scale for you, another for them.{/idea}
old: I am careful not to be cheated, and that is just being smart.
new: The fairness I demand for myself is the fairness I owe everyone else.
try: In your next split bill or transaction, round in the other person's favor.

title: Weigh with a straight balance.
subtitle: The scale itself must be honest
then: Shu'ayb told them to {idea}weigh with the true and straight balance.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes simply that {idea}the balance is the scales.{/idea} Honest weighing begins with an honest tool.
now: The scale is not always metal. It is the fine print on your contract, the hidden fee in your app, the rule you wrote that always favors you. {trap}A bent rule cheats every time it is used.{/trap}
old: As long as I am not lying outright, I am honest.
new: Honesty includes the systems and rules I set up, not just my words.
try: Look at one rule or arrangement you control at home or work. Check that it is fair both ways.

title: Do not shortchange people or spread corruption.
subtitle: Small cheating and open harm named together
then: Shu'ayb said: {trap}do not shortchange them{/trap}, and do not spread corruption in the land. Ibn Kathir explains the second as {trap}engaging in banditry{/trap}, like sitting on every road threatening people. The quiet thief and the open robber are named in one breath.
now: You would never rob anyone. But you leave work early on paid hours, use the company printer for personal stuff, skip paying back the small loan. {idea}It is the same habit, just quieter.{/idea}
old: Small unfairness is nothing like real crime.
new: Shortchanging people in small things grows from the same root as open harm.
try: Pay back one small thing you owe today, money, time, or a favor.

title: Fear the One who made you and all before you.
subtitle: The Creator of every generation
then: Shu'ayb warns them of {idea}Allah who created them and created their forefathers.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to Musa's words, {idea}your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers.{/idea} The ones they followed were also created and also answerable.
now: You look at old family photos: great-grandparents you never met. They lived, worked, traded, and are gone. {idea}The same Lord made them and made you.{/idea}
old: My forefathers set the rules I live by.
new: My forefathers and I answer to the same Creator.
try: Make dua today for your grandparents and those before them, by name if you know them.

title: Bewitched, they called him, just like Thamud did.
subtitle: Different peoples, the same excuse
then: Ibn Kathir notes Madyan responded {trap}like Thamud responded to their Messenger, for they were of like mind.{/trap} They said, {trap}you are one of those affected by witchcraft.{/trap} Centuries apart, refusal used the same words.
now: Notice your own excuses. They sound the same every time: I am too busy, it is not the right time, they are exaggerating. {idea}Same words, same refusal.{/idea}
old: My reasons for not changing are unique to my situation.
new: My excuses usually sound exactly like everyone else's.
try: Write down your most-used excuse. Next time you hear yourself say it, pause.

title: Just a man like us, and we think a liar.
subtitle: Suspicion as a defense

row.title: Allah chooses
sub: an ordinary man to carry truth

then: Madyan said {trap}we think you are deliberately lying to us, and Allah has not sent you.{/trap} Because he was a human like them, they could not accept he had a message. Quraysh said the same about the Prophet ﷺ.
now: Your younger sibling tells you something wise about your temper. Your first thought: who are you to tell me? {idea}Truth does not need an impressive messenger.{/idea}
old: I listen to advice from people above me, not people like me.
new: Truth can come through ordinary people, and I should not miss it because of who brings it.
try: Take one piece of advice seriously today from someone you usually would not.

title: Then bring down the sky on us.
subtitle: Daring the punishment out of stubbornness
then: They demanded {trap}a piece of the heaven to fall on them{/trap}, said in a stubborn, obstinate way. Ibn Kathir compares it to Quraysh, who said {trap}rain down stones on us{/trap} if this is the truth. The dare was meant to mock.
now: Someone warns you about where your spending is heading. You laugh: what, am I going to end up bankrupt? {idea}Laughing at a warning does not make it smaller.{/idea}
old: If I mock a warning, it shows I am not scared of it.
new: Mocking a warning is often how a heart avoids facing it.
try: Think of one warning you have joked about. Treat it seriously for five minutes today.

title: My Lord knows best what you do.
subtitle: Shu'ayb hands the matter back to Allah
then: Shu'ayb did not take the bait. He said {idea}my Lord is the best knower of what you do.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}if you deserve it, He will punish you, and He will not treat you unjustly.{/reward}
now: Someone provokes you in the comments, daring you to prove your point. You could fire back for an hour. {idea}Or you could say: Allah knows, and close the app.{/idea}
old: When someone dares me, I have to respond and win.
new: I can leave the final judgement to Allah, who knows and is never unjust.
try: Leave one argument today unanswered. Say to yourself: Allah knows best.

title: The cloud they ran to was the punishment.
subtitle: The Day of Shadow
then: They had asked for a piece of the sky to fall. Ibn Kathir says Allah sent {trap}intense heat{/trap}, then a cloud. They gathered beneath it for shade, and {trap}the punishment came from it.{/trap} It was {idea}an exact recompense{/idea} for what they had demanded.
now: The thing you run to for relief, the late-night scrolling, the shopping, the drink, feels like shade at first. {idea}Check what you are running toward.{/idea}
old: Whatever gives me relief right now must be good for me.
new: Not every shade is safe; real shelter is with Allah.
try: Next time you reach for quick relief today, pause and make a short dua instead first.

title: A sign for anyone who cheats on the scale.
subtitle: The refrain after Shu'ayb's story
then: The last of the seven stories ends here. A trading people who {trap}gave short measure and mocked their messenger{/trap} were taken. Then the refrain: {idea}in this is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.{/idea}
now: Every invoice, every online sale, every time you split costs with a roommate, you are holding a scale. {idea}Madyan's sign is about that moment.{/idea}
old: Stories of ancient nations are history, not about me.
new: Each story is a sign aimed at a habit I might share.
try: Review one recent deal you made. If it was unfair, make it right.

title: Mighty over the deniers, merciful to the believers.
subtitle: The last refrain of the seven stories
then: Ibn Kathir explains the refrain: {idea}He is All-Mighty in His punishment of the disbelievers{/idea}, and {reward}Most Merciful towards His believing servants.{/reward} After seven stories, the Prophet ﷺ is reminded once more who is in control.
now: You have just read story after story of people who ignored warnings. You might feel heavy. {reward}This is the reminder that the door of mercy is open to you right now.{/reward}
old: These stories just make me afraid.
new: The same Lord who is mighty is merciful to anyone who turns to Him.
try: End today with a short tawbah: ask Allah's forgiveness for one specific thing.

title: This Quran came from the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: After the stories, the source is named

row.title: the Quran
sub: a reminder from the Most Gracious

then: After seven stories of past nations, the surah turns to the Quran itself. Ibn Kathir says this refers back to the start, where it is called {reward}a Reminder from the Most Gracious.{/reward} {idea}Allah has sent it down to you and revealed it to you.{/idea}
now: The Quran app sits on your phone between social media and the weather. Same screen, same thumb. {idea}Only one of them came from the Lord of the worlds.{/idea}
old: The Quran is one good book among many.
new: The Quran is words sent down from the Lord of everything that exists.
try: Before reading any Quran today, pause and remember Who is speaking.

title: The trustworthy spirit carried it down.
subtitle: Jibril, the messenger to the messengers
then: The trustworthy Ruh is {reward}Jibril{/reward}, and Ibn Kathir says on this {idea}there is no dispute.{/idea} Every messenger in this surah said, I am a trustworthy messenger to you. Now the one who brought the Quran is called {reward}trustworthy{/reward} too.
now: You forward messages in the family group without checking. You pass on what you heard with a little added. {idea}The Quran reached you through a chain that never added or dropped a word.{/idea}
old: Passing information along is no big responsibility.
new: Carrying words faithfully is a trust, and the Quran came through the most trustworthy hands.
try: Before forwarding anything today, check it first.

title: Placed on his heart, so he could warn.
subtitle: The Quran lands on a heart first
then: Jibril brought it {reward}upon your heart, O Muhammad ﷺ, with nothing added or taken away.{/reward} Its purpose: {idea}to warn people of the punishment for opposing it, and to give glad tidings to the believers who follow it.{/idea}
now: You listen to recitation in the car, beautiful, half paying attention. It reaches your ears. {idea}The Quran was sent to reach the heart first.{/idea}
old: Hearing the Quran is enough.
new: The Quran is meant to land in my heart and then shape how I speak to others.
try: Pick one short verse today and let it sit in your heart by repeating it slowly.

title: In clear Arabic, leaving no room for excuses.
subtitle: A message made plain on purpose
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah revealed it {idea}in perfect and eloquent Arabic, so that it may be quite clear{/idea}, {trap}leaving no room for excuses{/trap}, establishing clear proof and showing the straight path. Quraysh understood every word.
now: You do not read Arabic, so you tell yourself the Quran is not really for you. Yet there is a translation on your phone right now. {idea}Clarity is one tap away.{/idea}
old: I cannot understand the Quran, so I am excused from it.
new: The Quran was made clear on purpose; my job is to open it.
try: Read the meaning of one short surah today in a language you understand well.

title: Foretold in the scriptures of those before.
subtitle: The Quran was expected, not invented
then: Ibn Kathir says this Quran {idea}was mentioned and referred to in the previous Scriptures{/idea}, foretold by their prophets. The last of them, 'Isa, {reward}gave the good news of a messenger named Ahmad.{/reward} Zubur here means books.
now: You treat your faith like something you happened to be born into, a family custom. {idea}It is the last chapter of a message prophets carried for thousands of years.{/idea}
old: Islam is just the religion I grew up with.
new: The Quran I hold was promised and awaited by prophets long before me.
try: Read 61:6 today and reflect on being part of what 'Isa gave glad tidings of.

title: The learned among the Children of Israel recognized it.
subtitle: Fair-minded scholars as witnesses
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the fair-minded among them admitted that the attributes of Muhammad ﷺ and his mission were mentioned in their Books.{/idea} Some believed, like {reward}'Abdullah bin Salam and Salman Al-Farisi.{/reward} This was a sign Quraysh could have looked at.
now: Someone with real expertise confirms something you have been resisting: the doctor, the accountant, the specialist. {idea}Being fair-minded means admitting what the evidence shows, even when it is inconvenient.{/idea}
old: I only accept truth from my own side.
new: Fair-mindedness means following what I know, wherever it leads.
try: Admit one thing today you know is true but have been resisting.

title: Even from a non-Arab, they would refuse.
subtitle: The excuse would only change shape
then: Ibn Kathir explains how {trap}intense the disbelief of Quraysh was.{/trap} If this eloquent Book had been revealed to {idea}a non-Arab who did not know one word of Arabic{/idea}, that would be an even greater wonder. They still would not have believed.
now: You say you would start praying if the mosque were closer, if the imam were better, if your schedule were freer. Change one thing and another reason appears. {idea}The excuse just moves.{/idea}
old: If the conditions were right, I would do it.
new: When one excuse is removed and another appears, the problem is the will, not the conditions.
try: Pick one good thing you keep postponing. Do it today under imperfect conditions.

title: Recited perfectly, and still not believed.
subtitle: A miracle cannot open a locked door
then: Ibn Kathir links this to other verses: {trap}even if a gate in the sky were opened, they would say our eyes are dazzled{/trap}; even if angels came and the dead spoke. The proof was never the problem.
now: Your friend shows you clear evidence that your plan will not work. You find a flaw in the font of the spreadsheet. {idea}When we do not want to see, we find reasons not to.{/idea}
old: With enough proof, anyone would be convinced.
new: Belief needs an open heart; proof alone cannot force it.
try: Ask Allah today to open your heart to any truth you have been resisting.

title: Denial settles into hearts that keep choosing it.
subtitle: What stubbornness becomes over time
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}thus We caused denial, disbelief, rejection and stubbornness to enter the hearts of the sinners.{/trap} The verse speaks of {idea}the criminals{/idea}, those who kept choosing wrong after the Quran came in clear Arabic.
now: The first time you lied to your boss, your heart raced. The tenth time, nothing. {trap}A heart that keeps refusing gets harder.{/trap} {idea}A heart that keeps turning back stays soft.{/idea}
old: I can always change my mind later, whenever I want.
new: Each time I refuse the truth, the next refusal comes easier, so turning back now matters.
try: Act today on one small truth your conscience is pressing you about, before it goes quiet.

title: They believe only once it is too late.
subtitle: Belief at the moment of punishment
then: They will not believe {trap}until they see the painful torment{/trap}, Ibn Kathir says, {trap}when their excuses will be of no avail.{/trap} He gives Fir'awn as the example: {idea}he only said I believe when drowning overtook him.{/idea}
now: You promise yourself you will get serious about prayer when you are older, after the kids grow up, after retirement. {idea}Belief means most when it is chosen before you are forced.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about faith when I need to.
new: Faith chosen freely, today, is worth what faith at the last moment is not.
try: Do one thing for your akhirah today that you had planned for later in life.

title: It comes suddenly, while they suspect nothing.
subtitle: No warning on the day itself
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}the punishment of Allah will come upon them suddenly{/trap}, while they do not perceive it. The warnings came for years through the messengers. {idea}The final moment itself would give no notice.{/idea}
now: People leave for work and do not come home. A young colleague, a healthy uncle, a neighbor. None of them knew it was the last morning. {idea}Neither will you.{/idea}
old: I will know when my time is getting close.
new: The end comes without notice, so the time to be ready is today.
try: Settle one thing today you would not want left undone: an apology, a debt, a call.

title: Could we have a little more time?
subtitle: The wish that comes too late
then: When they see the punishment, Ibn Kathir says, {trap}they will wish they had a little more time so that they can obey Allah, or so they claim.{/trap} {idea}When every sinner sees his punishment, he will feel intense regret.{/idea}
now: The time they will beg for is the time you have right now. This evening. This hour. {reward}The respite they ask for is already in your hands.{/reward}
old: I have plenty of time to fix things.
new: The extra time others will beg for is the time I am living in now.
try: Spend ten minutes today on the thing you would want more time for at the end.

title: Do they really want it to come sooner?
subtitle: Mocking the warning by asking for it
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}a denunciation and a threat{/trap}. Quraysh used to say to the Messenger ﷺ, {trap}bring Allah's torment upon us{/trap}, thinking it unlikely ever to happen. The same people would later ask for more time.
now: When someone warns you about your health, you joke: we all die of something. {idea}The joke is easy now; it will not feel the same in the hospital corridor.{/idea}
old: Joking about consequences shows I am not afraid.
new: Rushing toward what I do not believe in is the surest sign I have not thought about it.
try: Notice one thing you joke about to avoid taking seriously. Take it seriously for a moment.

title: Imagine years of enjoyment granted.
subtitle: A long life of comfort, considered
then: Allah invites a thought: {idea}have you considered{/idea} if We let them enjoy life for years? Ibn Kathir explains it as {idea}even if We delay the matter and give them respite for a short while or a long time.{/idea}
now: Things are going well. Promotions, a nice holiday, the house paid off. It is easy to read success as a sign that all is right with Allah. {idea}Comfort can also just be time.{/idea}
old: If my life is going well, I must be doing fine with Allah.
new: Years of comfort are respite, not a verdict.
try: In a moment of comfort today, ask yourself what you are doing with this time.

title: Then what was promised arrives.
subtitle: However long the delay, the promise comes
then: After the years of enjoyment, {idea}there came to them that which they were promised.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites 79:46: {idea}on the Day they see it, it will be as if they had stayed only an afternoon or a morning.{/idea}
now: Remember how fast the last ten years went. School, first job, wedding, kids. It felt long while living it. {idea}Looking back, it is an afternoon.{/idea}
old: I have a whole lifetime ahead before any of this matters.
new: A lifetime will feel like an afternoon when what was promised arrives.
try: Think of where you were ten years ago. Ask what you want to have done ten years from now.

title: All that enjoyment will not help them.
subtitle: Luxury cannot be carried forward

row.title: never saw good
sub: after one dip in the Fire
