then: Ibn Kathir asks: {trap}what good will their life of luxury do them then?{/trap} He cites an authentic hadith: the most comfortable disbeliever, dipped once in the Fire, says he never saw good. {reward}The most miserable believer, placed briefly in Paradise, says he never saw bad.{/reward}
now: You are stressed about the car you cannot afford, the life others post. Or you are hurting through a hard year. {reward}One moment of what is with Allah erases it all.{/reward}
old: My comfort or my hardship here is everything.
new: What I enjoy or suffer here is small next to what comes after.
try: If you are struggling today, tell Allah about it and ask Him for the better that is with Him.

title: No town was ever destroyed without warners.
subtitle: Allah's justice in every story
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}does not destroy any nation until after He has left them with no excuse{/idea}, by warning them and sending messengers. Every story in this surah showed it: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb each came first.
now: Think about how many reminders reach you in one week: a Friday khutbah, a verse on a friend's status, a funeral notice, your own conscience. {idea}You are being warned with care.{/idea}
old: I was never really told.
new: Allah has been sending me reminders all along, out of justice and care.
try: Write down three reminders that reached you this week. Respond to one of them.

title: A reminder first, and never any injustice.
subtitle: Warnings are meant to remind
then: The warners came {idea}by way of reminder{/idea}, and Allah says {reward}We have never been unjust.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes this is part of His justice towards His creation: {idea}warning them, sending messengers and establishing proof{/idea} before anything else.
now: A notification pops up: an old reminder you set to read Quran. You swipe it away. {idea}Every reminder is meant to bring you back, not to shame you.{/idea}
old: Religious reminders are there to make me feel guilty.
new: Reminders are mercy, given before any judgement, so I can return.
try: Set one small reminder on your phone today for a good habit, and keep it.

title: It was not the devils who brought it down.
subtitle: Answering the claim of magic and soothsaying
then: Quraysh called the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer. Allah answers: {trap}it is not the Shayatin who brought it down.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains the nature of devils is {trap}to corrupt and misguide{/trap}, while this Book {idea}enjoins what is right, forbids evil, and is light and guidance.{/idea}
now: You can judge a source by what it does to you. One feed leaves you anxious, jealous, angry. {idea}The Quran leaves you calmer and pointed toward good.{/idea}
old: All voices and sources are more or less the same.
new: What a message pushes me toward tells me where it came from.
try: Notice how you feel after ten minutes of your feed versus ten minutes of Quran today.

title: It would not suit them, and they could not.
subtitle: Two reasons the devils are not its source
then: Ibn Kathir explains: it {trap}would not suit them{/trap}, because the Quran {idea}enjoins what is right and forbids what is evil{/idea}, the opposite of what devils want. And {trap}they are not able{/trap}: had it been sent on a mountain, the mountain would have humbled itself from fear of Allah.
now: You read one verse and feel pulled to call your mother, forgive a friend, give in charity. {idea}That pull toward good tells you where those words came from.{/idea}
old: I cannot tell where any message really comes from.
new: Words that pull me toward good and away from harm carry the mark of their source.
try: Read one verse today and do the good it points you toward.

title: They were kept far from even hearing it.
subtitle: The Quran guarded while it came down
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the heavens were filled with guardians and shooting stars{/idea} while the Quran was revealed, {trap}so none of the Shayatin could hear even one letter of it.{/trap} He calls this {reward}part of Allah's mercy towards His servants.{/reward}
now: Everything you read online might be altered, edited, or faked. {reward}The Quran on your shelf was protected from the moment it came down.{/reward} You can trust every word.
old: Every text has been tampered with somewhere along the line.
new: The Quran was guarded from the first moment so I could rely on it fully.
try: Thank Allah today for one verse you love, knowing it reached you untouched.

title: Call on no other god besides Allah.
subtitle: The command given to the Prophet himself
then: After all the stories, Allah {idea}commands His Prophet ﷺ to worship Him alone, with no partner or associate{/idea}, and tells him that whoever associates others with Him will be punished. If the Prophet ﷺ is addressed this way, {idea}no one is exempt.{/idea}
now: You would never bow to an idol. But when you are worried, whose name do you reach for first: the boss, the bank, the doctor? {idea}Where does your heart go first?{/idea}
old: Shirk is something other people do with statues.
new: Turning to anyone before Allah in my heart is where the danger begins.
try: The next time you feel worried today, say a short dua before you call anyone.

title: Warn your closest family first.
subtitle: The Prophet climbed As-Safa and called out

row.title: I warn you
sub: of a punishment close at hand

row.title: only faith saves
sub: I cannot help you before Allah

then: When this was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ {idea}went to As-Safa, climbed up and called out{/idea} to the clans. He asked: if I told you a cavalry was behind this mountain, would you believe me? They said yes. He warned them. He also said to {reward}Fatimah and Safiyyah: I cannot help you before Allah.{/reward}
now: It is easier to give advice to strangers online than to your own brother at the dinner table. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ started with his family.{/idea}
old: My family will be fine because they are mine.
new: Caring for my family includes gently reminding them of what really saves.
try: Share one kind reminder with a family member today, in your own words.

title: Lower your wing to the believers who follow you.
subtitle: Gentleness toward those who are with you
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}commanded him to be kind and gentle with the believing servants of Allah who followed him.{/reward} In Makkah, his followers were often the poor, the young and the weak, mocked by the leaders. {idea}He was told to shelter them.{/idea}
now: The new member in your study circle, the junior at work who asks too many questions, the cousin just starting to pray. {reward}Lower your wing to them.{/reward}
old: People who are beginners should look up to me.
new: The higher my position, the lower my wing should be to those who follow.
try: Be extra patient today with one person who is newer at something than you.

title: If they refuse, say: I am free of what you do.
subtitle: Separating yourself from the deed

row.title: the deed
sub: what you do, not who you are

then: Allah told him to {idea}disown those who disobeyed him, no matter who they were.{/idea} The words are precise: {idea}I am innocent of what you do.{/idea} The deed is rejected; the warning was already given.
now: Your friend wants your help hiding something from his wife. You can stay his friend and still say: I will not be part of this. {idea}Separate from the deed, not the person.{/idea}
old: Loyalty means going along with whatever my people do.
new: I can stay close to people while clearly refusing to share in their wrong.
try: Say no kindly to one request today that would pull you into something wrong.

title: Rely on the Mighty, the Merciful.
subtitle: The refrain's two names become a place to lean
then: The two names that closed every story now become {reward}the ones to trust{/reward}. Ibn Kathir: {reward}in all your affairs, for He is your Helper, Protector and Supporter{/reward}, and {idea}He will make your word supreme.{/idea}
now: You did the hard thing: spoke the truth to family, quit the wrong job, refused the bribe. Now you feel alone. {reward}Lean on the One who is mighty enough to help and merciful enough to want to.{/reward}
old: After doing right, I am on my own.
new: When I do right, the Mighty and Merciful is the one I lean on.
try: After one hard decision today, say: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: He sees you when you stand.
subtitle: Watched over, especially in prayer
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}He is taking care of you{/reward}, linking it to {reward}you are under Our eyes.{/reward} Ibn Abbas said it means standing {idea}to pray{/idea}; Al-Hasan said {idea}when you pray alone{/idea}; Qatadah said in every situation.
now: The night prayer no one knows about. The two rakahs in an empty office stairwell. Nobody saw. {reward}He saw you stand.{/reward}
old: Prayer no one sees does not count for much.
new: The Lord I trust sees me every time I stand for Him, even alone.
try: Pray two extra rakahs today where no one can see.

title: And your movements among those who prostrate.
subtitle: Seen in the row of worshippers
then: Qatadah explained: {reward}He sees you when you pray alone and when you pray in congregation.{/reward} 'Ikrimah said He sees him {idea}when he stands and bows and prostrates.{/idea} Every movement of the Prophet ﷺ among the worshippers was seen.
now: Jumuah, a packed mosque, hundreds in rows. You feel like a small dot among them. {reward}Your one sujood is seen exactly, not as part of a crowd.{/reward}
old: In a big crowd, my prayer is just one among many.
new: Allah sees each movement of mine, even in the fullest row.
try: In your next prayer, make one sujood longer and more present than usual.

title: He alone hears everything and knows everything.
subtitle: Nothing you say or do goes unnoticed
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}He hears all that His servants say and He knows all their movements.{/idea} He cites 10:61: {reward}you do no deed, and recite no portion of the Quran, but We are witness to it.{/reward} This closes the comfort given to the Prophet ﷺ.
now: You whisper a dua in the car between meetings, barely moving your lips. You wonder if it even counts. {reward}It was heard completely.{/reward}
old: My quiet prayers probably do not reach anywhere.
new: Every whisper is heard and every effort is known.
try: Whisper one honest dua today in a spare moment, trusting it is heard.

title: Shall I tell you who the devils come down on?
subtitle: Answering the claim the Quran came from jinn
then: Ibn Kathir says idolaters claimed the Prophet's ﷺ message {trap}came to him in visions from the Jinn.{/trap} Allah answers with a question. Devils {trap}descend upon those who are like them, the lying fortune-tellers{/trap}, and he was nothing like them.
now: You can usually tell what is shaping someone by looking at their life. The same works on yourself. {idea}What kind of voices are drawn to you?{/idea}
old: Who influences me does not say much about me.
new: The voices that settle on me show what I have made room for.
try: Unfollow or mute one source today that usually leaves you worse.

title: They descend on every lying sinner.
subtitle: Lies and immoral deeds attract them
then: Ibn Kathir explains the two words: {trap}one whose speech is lies and fabrication, and whose deeds are immoral.{/trap} That is the fortune-teller. Makkah knew the Prophet ﷺ was the opposite: {reward}honest in speech and upright in conduct.{/reward}
now: Small lies to get out of plans. A little exaggeration in your CV. Gossip passed along. {trap}Each one opens a door a little wider.{/trap}
old: Small lies are harmless.
new: Lying and wrongdoing make a person a home for the wrong kind of whispers.
try: Go one full day without a single small lie, even to be polite.

title: One stolen word, a hundred lies.
subtitle: How fortune-tellers seem right
then: Ibn Kathir explains they try to overhear the heavens, then {trap}add to it a hundred lies{/trap}. People believe all of it because one thing came true. Asked about fortune-tellers, the Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}they are nothing.{/idea}
now: A horoscope app, a viral prediction, a guru who was right once. One hit and people trust everything after. {idea}One true word does not make the rest true.{/idea}
old: If someone predicted something correctly, they must know.
new: One correct word can carry a hundred lies with it.
try: Delete or ignore one prediction or horoscope source you check out of habit.

title: The poets, and the lost who follow them.
subtitle: Why the Prophet was not a poet
then: Quraysh called the Prophet ﷺ a poet; the surah is named after this verse. 'Ikrimah said {trap}two poets would ridicule one another in verse, with one group supporting one and another group the other.{/trap} Allah says: {idea}We have not taught him poetry.{/idea}
now: Two people fight in the comments, each with fans cheering. Clever insults, likes, screenshots. {trap}The crowd follows whoever is wittiest, not whoever is right.{/trap}
old: Whoever argues best online must be right.
new: Following the cleverest voice is not the same as following the truth.
try: Next time you see an online fight today, scroll past without picking a side.

title: Wandering in every valley of words.
subtitle: Talk with no fixed direction
then: Ibn Abbas said {trap}they indulge in every kind of nonsense{/trap}, and also that {trap}they engage in every kind of verbal art.{/trap} They wander from praise to insult to boasting with no fixed truth. {idea}The Quran is a reminder with one direction.{/idea}
now: You post about everything: hot takes, rants, opinions you will change next week. {idea}How much of what you said this month was true and useful?{/idea}
old: Having an opinion on everything shows I am engaged.
new: Words that wander everywhere rarely lead anyone anywhere good.
try: Skip giving one opinion today that you do not really need to give.

title: They say what they do not do.
subtitle: The gap between words and life
then: The poets {trap}say what they do not do.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the Messenger ﷺ was not a poet {idea}because his situation was quite obviously different to theirs.{/idea} He did what he taught, and Makkah could see it.
now: Your status says be grateful; your evening was spent complaining. You told your kids to stop yelling, while yelling. {idea}Close the gap a little.{/idea}
old: Saying the right things is most of the job.
new: My words weigh only as much as the life behind them.
try: Pick one thing you often tell others to do. Do it yourself today.

title: Except those who believe and use their words well.
subtitle: The door for every tongue to turn

row.title: good wipes out bad
sub: new words make up for old

then: Ibn Kathir says this includes poets who once mocked Islam, then {reward}repented, did good and remembered Allah much, to make up for what they said{/reward}. 'Abdullah bin Az-Zab'ari said: {reward}my tongue will try to make up for what it said.{/reward} The surah ends: {trap}the wrongdoers will come to know their return.{/trap}
now: Think of the harsh things you have said, typed, posted. They cannot be unsaid. {reward}They can be outweighed by better words from today on.{/reward}
old: What I said in the past defines me.
new: My tongue can turn and make up for what it once said, by remembering Allah and speaking good.
try: Send one kind message today to someone you once spoke badly to or about.
